entries.crumb: CodeSense — Roles: role_save, roles_list and queue configuration
entries.text: Roles: queue settings and live holders. role: builder exclusive · one holder queue persists across holders amelia-1 session · exited amelia-2 session · live amelia-3 session · pending register_role (current) waits for release next holder on release release_role The seat moves between sessions. The queue stays.

entries.title: Four seat moves
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Roles: role_save, roles_list and queue configuration
entries.text: Four seat moves 1 Register An agent joins the queue. Use exclusive: true for a single holder, such as a resolver; omit it for a shared worker pool. An exclusive registration returns alreadyHeld if someone else is already there. // MCP tool: register_role {"team":{"org":"acme","team":"dev"},"role":"manager","sessionId":"YOUR_SESSION_ID","exclusive":true} 2 Claim Pull a batch off the role's queue. Each delivery hands back a deliveryId + claimToken you'll need to accept and ack. // MCP tool: claim_role_messages — use instanceId and generation from register_role {"team":{"org":"acme","team":"dev"},"role":"manager","instanceId":"YOUR_INSTANCE_ID","generation":1,"limit":10} 3 Hand off You don't literally hand the role to another session; you just reply with replyTo: "role:manager" . The reply lands on the role queue, so whoever's holding it next picks it up. The thread survives the handoff. 4 Release When the human says stop, finish the current delivery, then release_role . Claimed-but-not-accepted work goes back to pending for the next holder. CodeSense also releases automatically when the session ends. // MCP tool: release_role — use instanceId and generation from register_role {"team":{"org":"acme","team":"dev"},"role":"manager","instanceId":"YOUR_INSTANCE_ID","generation":1}

entries.title: What a role is
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Roles: role_save, roles_list and queue configuration
entries.text: A role is a named queue. Registrations are shared by default, so several sessions can claim work from it. When an agent calls register_role {role: "builder", exclusive: true} , it becomes the exclusive builder for the lifetime of that session; another holder's attempt returns alreadyHeld instead of silently clobbering. The queue outlives any particular holder — if you kill the session, the next one that registers picks up exactly where the last one left off, including work that was accepted but not yet acked.

entries.title: Worked example — manager-wake
entries.text: Worked example — manager-wake The seed examples/agents/manager/routines/manager-wake/routine.yml lives under the Manager agent and wakes it when mail waits. Short, declarative, no polling. id: manager-wake name: Wake the manager owner: codesense mode: wake task: | You have unread mail. Call read_messages with your session id, then claim_role_messages for the manager role, and carry on with /manage-team. If there is nothing for you, say so in one line and wait. where: kind: team_workspace machine: local triggers: - event: kind: inbox_idle policy: max_runtime: 5m runs_on: each_mac revision: 1

entries.title: Wake on idle.
entries.text: Wake on idle. role: builder queue pending · msg #1 pending · msg #2 routine event: inbox_idle idle with mail amelia-builder idle → woken → claims fires mode: wake No central scheduler — the queue's silence is the signal.

entries.title: Two shapes of trigger
entries.text: Two shapes of trigger event-driven — triggers: [{event: {kind: inbox_idle}}] fires as a reaction. Zero cost when the queue is quiet; immediate when work lands. Use this for anything the inbox can notify. cron-driven — triggers: [{schedule: {cron: "0 * * * *"}}] fires on a wall-clock cadence. Pair with event-driven when you need a liveness backstop. The seed manager-ensure wakes the Manager every hour to check its queue (starting one if none runs); manager-wake uses the event to wake it when mail waits. Both routines consult the same queue state via the same MCP tools; one is reactive, one is a safety net. You get a system that's quiet when nothing's happening, instant when something is, and self-healing when a machine was asleep.

entries.title: What inbox_idle is
entries.text: You don't want workers polling. You don't want a central scheduler. You want a sleeping agent to wake exactly when there's work on its queue — nothing before, nothing after. inbox_idle is the trigger that does that: a routine declares event.kind: inbox_idle , and CodeSense fires it when a session sits idle at its prompt with unread mail. With mode: wake only the routine's own agent's sessions fire it, and CodeSense types its task into the one with the mail — the Manager, say — and the loop in manage-team picks the work up. No second agent does the waking, and a worker's mail never wakes the Manager.

entries.title: The two files
entries.text: The two files The routine lives under the agent it wakes, so it names no agent: . Both files ship in these docs under examples/agents/manager/ . config/agents/manager/agent.yaml id: manager name: Manager description: Watches the manager role queue, triages incoming work, launches and tracks workers, and reports to you. runtime: claude launch: foreground startup: - CLAUDE.md - .claude/skills/manage-team/ default_prompt: /manage-team revision: 1 config/agents/manager/routines/manager-wake/routine.yml id: manager-wake name: Wake the manager owner: codesense mode: wake task: | You have unread mail. Call read_messages with your session id, then claim_role_messages for the manager role, and carry on with /manage-team. If there is nothing for you, say so in one line and wait. where: kind: team_workspace machine: local triggers: - event: kind: inbox_idle policy: max_runtime: 5m runs_on: each_mac revision: 1

entries.title: Wake the Manager.
entries.text: Arc G · Routines Wake the Manager. The routine wakes the agent it belongs to. Nothing in between. manager · unread mail role: manager · DEMO-2 role: manager · DEMO-3 reply · from Barb manager-wake mode: wake event: inbox_idle Manager (its own tab) idle → woken → claims fires types when idle Woken by Wake the manager

entries.title: What happens, step by step
entries.text: What happens, step by step Mail arrives. A message lands in the Manager session's inbox — a worker's report, a question for it. The Manager is idle at its prompt. Its inbox waiter tells it at once, but if it leaves the mail unread (or runs without a waiter), nothing tells it again. The event fires. One of the Manager's own sessions sits idle with unread mail, so inbox_idle fires manager-wake (at most once every 30 seconds). Mail waiting for another agent — a worker, an ad-hoc tab — never fires a Manager's wake routine; give that agent its own. CodeSense finds the Manager. It looks for the Manager's live session on the routine's machine , preferring the one with the mail, then an idle one. Local sessions must be tagged as launched for this routine. It waits for a quiet moment. It types only when the agent is idle, no one has typed in that tab for 3 seconds, and no permission prompt is waiting. Then it pastes the task once, headed [routine: Wake the manager | run <id>] , and submits it. You can see it. The tab's caption says "Woken by Wake the manager" and the scrollback gets a marker. The run is recorded delivered . The Manager works. It reads and claims, then may call routine_done with the run id to record a result for that run, while its session carries on.

entries.title: No middleman
entries.text: No middleman Before routines could wake, the pattern was a second, short-lived agent whose task called list_sessions and send_to_session to nudge the real one. Don't write that any more: mode: wake delivers into the agent the routine belongs to, waits for it to be idle, never collides with your typing, and records an honest result. send_to_session is still the tool for an agent nudging another agent by hand. For "check back on this in 20 minutes" from inside a session, don't write a routine at all: set a timer on that session.

entries.title: Busy, absent, on another machine
entries.text: Busy, absent, on another machine Busy: the run is queued ("Waiting for Manager to be idle") and delivered at its next idle point, up to the routine's max wait (30 minutes by default), else undelivered (busy_timeout) . Fires that come meanwhile fold into it ( coalesced ). Not running: it starts the Manager with the task as its first prompt. On this Mac, only one start is in flight per routine, so repeated fires of that routine never start two Managers. Separate local routines get separate sessions. Remote starts keep their existing per-agent/workspace admission. On a connected machine: set machine to its id, or any to wake the agent wherever it runs (starting it on this Mac when none does). The machine itself delivers, so a wake lands even if the desktop drops while it waits. A machine that is offline gives undelivered (machine_offline) , never a second Manager. Unknown: when CodeSense can't confirm the text went in, the run says "May have been delivered. Check the terminal before re-sending." It is never re-sent automatically, and it posts once to your inbox. Ignored: after 3 wakes that leave the same mail unread, the routine stops waking for that mail and raises "needs you".

entries.title: Try this now
entries.text: Try this now With the Manager copied into your editable context repo, fire its wake routine once by hand. If the Manager is running, the task goes into its tab; if not, a Manager starts.

entries.title: How to do this via MCP
entries.text: How to do this via MCP // A wake routine on a saved agent, every weekday at 9 codesense.invoke('routine_create', { name: 'Morning triage', agent: 'barb', mode: 'wake', when: 'weekdays 09:00', task: 'Triage new issues, then call routine_done with a one-line summary.', }) // Fire it once, then read how it went (delivered / queued / undelivered / unknown) codesense.invoke('routine_run_now', { id: 'morning-triage' }) codesense.invoke('routine_runs', { id: 'morning-triage', limit: 5 }) // Inside the woken session: finish just this run, keep working codesense.invoke('routine_done', { sessionId, runId, outcome: 'success', summary: '4 triaged' })

entries.title: Who can be woken
entries.text: Who can be woken A saved agent with launch: foreground . The built-in starters ( builtin/claude , builtin/codex ) start a new session only, so a tab someone opened by hand is never typed into. A headless run is never woken. An agent that auto-approves every tool needs allowWake: true in its definition. Codex idle detection isn't qualified yet, so wakes into Codex sessions may come back undelivered (unobservable) . The wake text is the task with only {{date}} and {{timestamp}} filled in; {{last_run_summary}} and {{trigger.*}} are for start-a-new runs.

entries.title: Wake or start a new — what a routine fire does
entries.text: Every routine has a mode . wake types the routine's task into a matching running session once it is idle, so the agent keeps everything it already knows. On this Mac, the session must carry this routine's launch tag: another routine's session or an untagged Agents-tab session is never adopted. Each local routine starts its own session when none matches. Remote wakes retain per-agent/workspace matching and admission for now. start a new ( mode: fresh in the file) starts a new session of the agent on every fire, with the task as its whole prompt. A Manager, a triage desk or a long-lived Builder you keep open and talk to wants wake . A nightly report or a digest that wants a clean slate wants start a new . A wake with no running session doesn't fail: it starts one, with the task as its first prompt. So one routine both keeps a live agent busy and brings it back when it is gone.

entries.title: Metadata → command → agent
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Command routines: argv commands and an agent chain
entries.text: Metadata → command → agent A story changing from in-progress to review fires the command. On its successful completion, an agent gets the stdout as its task input. Save the command first, then the agent routine; the predecessor must exist in the same space. after.routine is its bare routine id. Chains reject cycles. on: succeeded continues only after success; on: finished continues after succeeded , failed , timed_out , needs_you or ended ; cancelled does not fire a chain. An independent schedule or event may coexist with an after trigger. Choose a saved agent id for the final step (the example uses default ). Dry-run both blocks, save them with dryRun:false , inspect with routine_get , then enable both. If installing the YAML by hand, arm each one_mac definition with routine_arm_on {id, machine:"this_mac"} before enabling; preserve the placement of MCP-created drafts. Existing metadata matches are baselined, so make a new controlled transition after enabling. The command receives {{trigger.path}} as a separate argv element and prints that original document path. Its stdout reaches the agent as {{trigger.result_text}} , so the agent can open the exact changed story. Replace the print step with your validator while preserving that identity in its output. Metadata review command MCP: routine_create dry run { "maxRuntime": "5m", "enabled": false, "dryRun": true, "id": "review-command", "name": "Metadata review command", "action": "command", "command": [ "python3", "-c", "import sys; print(sys.argv[1])", "{{trigger.path}}" ], "metadataTriggers": [ { "selection": { "where": { "kinds": [ "story" ] } }, "target": { "key": "status", "op": "eq", "value": "review" }, "previous": { "key": "status", "op": "eq", "value": "in-progress" } } ] } Complete routine.yml id: "review-command" name: "Metadata review command" owner: "codesense" where: kind: "team_workspace" policy: max_runtime: "5m" overlap: "queue" revision: 1 action: "command" command: - "python3" - "-c" - "import sys; print(sys.argv[1])" - "{{trigger.path}}"…

entries.title: command routine action command argv no shell
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Command routines: argv commands and an agent chain
entries.text: Use a command routine for deterministic work: validate a file, run a script, collect a small report. Use an agent routine when the work needs judgment, tools selected by the agent, or a conversation. A command routine launches no agent and makes no model call. Set action: command and an argv array: the program is the first element, each argument is its own element. Omit agent , task and mode . Commands have no wake mode and run on this Mac. They live under config/agents/_command/routines/<id>/routine.yml . command: [python3, scripts/check-review.py, --format, json] The program may be a name found on PATH or a path inside the team's files; absolute program paths, parent traversal and whitespace in the program name are refused. Prefer python3 scripts/check-review.py or node scripts/check-review.mjs as separate argv entries because sync does not preserve executable permission. Pipes, redirects and shell expansion are not interpreted. The working directory follows where.kind : team_workspace uses the team content root, while repo:owner/repo uses that managed repository clone. Relative program paths in argv[0] still resolve under the team content root. Each template expands within one argv element; it is never split into shell words.

entries.title: Outputs and outcomes
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Command routines: argv commands and an agent chain
entries.text: Outputs and outcomes Exit 0 records succeeded ; a nonzero code records failed . Cancellation and a runtime deadline record cancelled and timed_out . Use routine_runs then routine_run for the exit code, stdout/stderr tails, argv and working directory. Captured output is bounded (4096-byte tails), so save large artifacts to a file. The child receives CODESENSE_ROUTINE_ID and CODESENSE_RUN_ID . Stdout becomes the run's result_text . A chained routine reads it as {{trigger.result_text}} ; also available are {{trigger.run_id}} , {{trigger.routine}} , {{trigger.phase}} and {{trigger.detail}} . result_text is what the command produced; detail is CodeSense's explanation of why the run ended (a command that did not start, such as unresolved:itemId ). Wake, machine and admission runs still explain themselves in result_text . Command stdout is plain result text; result_schema does not parse or validate it as a structured published payload.

entries.title: Cancel one run
entries.text: Cancel one run An agent calls routine_cancel {runId} to cancel one queued or running run. Read routine_runs first and use the returned run_id : routine_runs {"id":"acme/api/backend/digest","limit":20} // Choose a queued or running row and copy its run_id. routine_cancel {"runId":"<run_id from routine_runs>"} routine_run {"runId":"<the same run_id>"} Success returns {status:"ok", data:{routine_id, routine_name, run_id, phase, created_at, started_at, ended_at, ...}} , the same row shape as routine_run , with RFC3339 times. Cancelling a fresh run stops its agent or command. Cancelling a wake run keeps the session it woke alive; queued wake text is withdrawn from its host first. If the host already delivered it, the response reports that it could not be withdrawn and gives its actual phase. An unreachable host or a remote launch still starting returns an error; the run stays queued. An unknown run, a run outside your visible routines, or an already finished run returns validation with a message; finished runs are unchanged. Shared team runs can be cancelled regardless of who created the routine. MCP identity comes from the verified connection; omit sessionId , or supply only your own. An unbound connection or another caller's id is refused. This cancels one run and leaves future fires enabled. Other queued runs may start when this one ends. To pause future starts, use routine_set_enabled {id, enabled:false} . The pane method codesense.routineCancel({key}) is a different operation: it batch-cancels this principal's live structured-result attempts for that routine and returns a count, retaining last-good data. See troubleshooting .

entries.title: Trigger shapes
entries.text: Trigger shapes A trigger is a schedule (a cron and a time zone) or an event . The event kinds are inbox_idle , role_pending and agent_done . No triggers means manual only. inbox_idle Fires when a session sits idle at its prompt with unread mail. With mode: wake it wakes the routine's own agent. Zero cost when nothing waits; immediate when work lands. The glue of the inbox-driven factory. schedule A standard 5-field cron in a time zone (an agent can also pass a preset such as daily 09:00 as when ). Fires on wall-clock cadence. Great for liveness backstops, synthesis passes, or a nightly sweep. manual Fires only when a human clicks Run now , a dashboard's Refresh calls routineRefresh , or an agent calls routine_run_now . The docs' own update-codesense-docs routine is one: the Update button runs it. agent_done Fires when an agent finishes ( signal_done ), optionally only one agent ( from_agent ). The routine shows under the agent it runs, with an "after ‹agent›" note. role_pending Fires once for each message queued for a role inbox. A controller routine uses it to start an agent for the role, which then claims the message. The run gets {{trigger.role}} and {{trigger.message_id}} . each_mac Not a trigger by itself — a runs_on scope that pairs with any of the above. The routine fires once per trusted Mac on each tick, so remote fleets stay independent.

entries.text: How to do this via MCP // Every routine you can see, or one agent's codesense.invoke('routine_list', {}) codesense.invoke('routine_list', { agent: 'manager' }) // Make one for Barb: wake her running session every weekday at 9 codesense.invoke('routine_create', { name: 'Morning triage', agent: 'barb', mode: 'wake', when: 'weekdays 09:00', task: '…', }) // Or, for your own session only, a timer codesense.invoke('schedule_wakeup', { sessionId, in: '20m', prompt: '…' }) // Fire a routine once by hand codesense.invoke('routine_run_now', { id: 'manager-wake' }) See mcp-explorer for the full tool catalog.

entries.title: What a routine is — a schedule-shape, not a daemon
entries.text: A routine is a saved agent's standing task: a tiny bit of YAML, stored under that agent, that pairs a trigger with a task . The trigger is "when" (a schedule, an idle inbox, mail queued for a role, another agent finishing, a human clicking Run ). The mode is "how": wake types the task into the agent's running session when it is idle (starting one only if none runs), and start a new ( mode: fresh ) starts a new session every time. No daemon, no polling — CodeSense owns the clock. In the app, routines live in the Agents tab: each agent's Routines section, and the Agents | Schedule view. For "do this later" inside one conversation there is a lighter tool: a session timer , a temporary routine that comes back to that same session and ends with it.

entries.title: Routines on remote machines.
entries.text: Arc G · Routines Routines on remote machines. One routine on disk. Different firing shapes per Mac. nightly-digest.yml scope: team · runs_on: each_mac Sam's MacBook armed · fires at 09:00 his inbox, his context Mac asleep → skipped Build box (remote) armed · always on remote-owned context never skips Teammate's Mac off · no fires armed_here: false starts off everywhere Per-Mac switch (routine_set_enabled). Local change. Never a git edit.

entries.title: Wake an agent that runs on another machine
entries.text: Wake an agent that runs on another machine runs_on says which Mac's clock fires a routine. where.machine says where its agent is: local (this Mac, the default), a machine id from list_machines , or any connected machine. Wake on a machine. The desktop hands the task to that machine, and the machine types it into the agent's session when it is idle. The wait happens there, so the wake still lands if your desktop drops meanwhile. Nobody running there. A wake starts the agent on that machine, in its prepared workspace, with the task as its first prompt. any with no agent running anywhere starts it on this Mac. Machine offline. A session last seen there still counts as live, so nothing starts a duplicate: the run is undelivered (machine_offline) and the next fire tries again. A machine this desktop doesn't know is undelivered (machine_unknown) , with a fix. An old terminal server. Wakes and timers need a current one; the run says "Update the terminal server on ‹machine›". config/agents/amelia-builder/routines/builder-wake/routine.yml id: builder-wake name: Wake the Builder on the build box owner: you mode: wake task: | Claim the next story with claim_role_messages for the builder role and carry on with /bmad-build. Nothing pending: say so and wait. where: kind: team_workspace machine: build-box # a machine id from list_machines triggers: - schedule: cron: "*/30 * * * *" tz: UTC policy: max_runtime: 30m revision: 1 Reading how it went codesense.invoke('routine_runs', { id: 'builder-wake', limit: 5 }) // → delivered | queued | coalesced // | undelivered (machine_offline, busy_timeout, …) // | unknown (never re-sent: check the terminal first) With runs_on , an each_mac routine must use machine: local (or leave it out), except that a fresh one may use any (each Mac starts its own); a machine id is refused in either mode, since every teammate's Mac would wake or start the same agent there. To have the machine's own clock fire a routine, arm it there with routine_arm_on and a machine id: its terminal server fires it on…

entries.title: Two modes: each_mac vs one_mac
entries.text: Two modes: each_mac vs one_mac runs_on: each_mac A recipe each teammate turns on for their own Mac. Fires per Mac that armed it, each with its own schedule, its own history, and its own {{last_run_summary}} . Starts off on every Mac — including the author's — unless the routine ships with enabled: true . Use for per-person work: "my morning digest", "PRs waiting on me". Use for inbox_idle wakes (sessions are per Mac). Use for sweeping remote fleets — one definition, N independent fires. runs_on: one_mac (the default) A shared job that runs once for the team, from exactly one Mac — the one it was armed on. Perfect for anything that must happen once (a Slack digest, a release-cut check), and the thing that should move to the always-on remote box when you want "never skipped". Use for team-wide must-fire schedules. Arm it on the remote account for always-on behavior. Switching the arming Mac is a routine_update from the target Mac.

entries.title: Parity caveats
entries.text: Parity caveats Three rows from the Arc-D parity matrix describe how remote routines differ from local ones: Run a routine — ✓ local, ⚠ remote. Caveat: a routine fires in the account that owns the triggering workspace. If you want "always on", own the routine on the always-on machine. Routine schedule (cron) — ✓ local, ⚠ remote. Local Macs skip fires while asleep (standard Mac behavior); remote always-on boxes never skip. Workaround: own must-fire schedules on the remote. Wake and timers — ✓ both. A remote session is woken, and its timers fire, by the machine it runs on, with the same idle and no-collision rules as a local one. See agent wake and session timers .

entries.title: The per-Mac switch
entries.text: The per-Mac switch enabled on a routine is a per-Mac field: it names whether this Mac fires the routine. Flipping it is routine_set_enabled , which is a local edit to the Mac's state (never a git change, never shared). // Turn the routine on for THIS Mac codesense.invoke('routine_set_enabled', { id: 'builder-wake', enabled: true }) // Turn it off for THIS Mac — other Macs that armed it are unaffected codesense.invoke('routine_set_enabled', { id: 'builder-wake', enabled: false }) // Which Macs is it armed on? routine_get on each; each Mac answers for itself. codesense.invoke('routine_get', { id: 'builder-wake' }) // → { ..., armed_here: true, next_run_at: "2026-10-06T19:05:00Z" } For a one_mac routine, exactly one Mac has armed_here: true at a time. Switching the arming Mac is a routine_update from the target — "pull the arming to this Mac", not a flip on the current one.

entries.title: Try this now
entries.text: Try this now List every routine on the active team along with its mode and arming state. The response includes runs_on and armed_here for each, so you can see at a glance which fires where.

entries.title: How to do this via MCP
entries.text: How to do this via MCP // Every routine, each Mac's arming state codesense.invoke('routine_list', {}) // A specific routine, with armed_here + next_run_at from THIS Mac's view codesense.invoke('routine_get', { id: 'builder-wake' }) // Flip this Mac's per-Mac switch (local, never a git change) codesense.invoke('routine_set_enabled', { id: 'builder-wake', enabled: true }) // Move the arming of a one_mac routine to THIS Mac codesense.invoke('routine_update', { id: 'nightly-digest', baseRevision: 3, armHere: true, }) // Fire it once (through its own overlap rule) codesense.invoke('routine_run_now', { id: 'builder-wake' })

entries.title: Why remote routines are their own concern
entries.text: A routine's YAML sits in the context repo and syncs with every teammate. The firing , though, is per Mac — because a Mac is where the wall clock ticks, where the inbox lives, and where the agent spawns. Remote routines (ones that run on a build box or a teammate's always-on machine) use the same YAML as local routines; the only knobs that change are runs_on (the mode) and armed_here (this Mac's local switch). The Arc-D parity matrix treats routine schedules as the main caveat row — remote scheduling is strictly better than local for anything "always on".

entries.title: Wake an agent that runs on another machine
Author a definition
entries.text: Author a definition Give every routine a unique team-wide id , nonblank name and owner , where.kind and policy.max_runtime (1m–24h). Start revision at 1; saves increment it. A field default in the wire schema does not imply the resulting definition passes semantic validation. action: agent is the default. Give it a nonblank task . Usually omit agent because its directory supplies it. Legacy and unassigned files can carry a bare or scoped agent reference. mode: wake delivers into a matching idle saved agent's session and starts one only if none matches. On this Mac, the session must carry this routine's launch identity . fresh starts a new session. A blank mode is resolved at fire time; read effective_mode in the tool reply. Built-in starters are fresh only. Bypass agents need allowWake: true . action: command needs command as argv, and no agent, task or mode. Commands run on this Mac, without a model. See command routines . where.kind is team_workspace or repo:owner/repo . where.machine is local, any, or a machine id for agent routines. runs_on defaults to one_mac; each_mac is a per-Mac opt-in recipe. Metadata triggers refuse each_mac. triggers contains singleton schedule or event maps. Empty means manual. after: {routine: review-command, on: succeeded} adds a same-space dependency; finished continues after succeeded , failed , timed_out , needs_you or ended ; cancelled does not fire a chain. See the six trigger recipes . policy.overlap is coalesce, skip or queue (MCP command creation defaults to queue). policy.missed is skip or run_once. policy.visible opens a fresh agent in a tab; wakes are visible. policy.max_wakes , max_wakes_per_day and min_gap limit deliveries into live sessions. Positive counts only; min_gap is 1m–7d. Reaching the total pauses the routine; daily limits recover automatically. Fresh runs ignore wake limits with a warning. policy.max_wait is a supported wake-runner extension stored in the policy’s extra fields. It bounds how long a wake waits for an idle session: 30 minutes by default; use a…

entries.title: Role queue filters
entries.text: Role queue filters Use {kind:"role_pending"} when a dispatcher needs every role queue in reach. Use {kind:"role_pending",role:"reviewer"} when this routine should run only for reviewer mail. triggers: - event: kind: role_pending role: reviewer Omit role for the wildcard. A team routine reaches only its team; a private routine reaches teams in its org. Empty or whitespace-only role values fail validation, and role is valid only on role_pending . Role names need no registry entry. agent_done alone accepts from_agent (id or full key, no existence check). MCP uses the same spelling inside events . Updating with null or omitted events preserves; [] clears these three event kinds; a nonempty list replaces them and keeps schedules/metadata triggers. Only creation supports dryRun , which reports resolved triggers and writes no definition.

entries.title: Generated fields
entries.text: Generated fields Nested rows show their full wire paths. A nested field marked optional may still be required inside an optional parent object; the JSON Schema records those conditional requirements exactly. Field Wire type Presence Description action string optional after object | null optional after.on string optional after.routine string optional agent string optional The agent that runs the task; see [`AgentRef`]. A routine stored under its agent (`config/agents/<agent>/routines/<id>/`) does not write it: the path names the agent and every read fills it in (`layout`). Only a legacy `config/routines/<id>/` file or an `_unassigned` one carries it. archived_at string | null optional archived_with_agent boolean optional Archived because its agent was archived: restoring the agent offers to restore exactly these (`lifecycle`). arm_epoch integer optional Bumped on every move of the routine between a desktop and a machine. A machine refuses an arm or disarm older than the epoch it holds, so a stale definition can never re-arm it there. armed_host string optional The local host id of the one Mac that arms this routine, so it fires once however many machines have it. Placement, not permission: anyone may move it. Unset only in a definition written outside CodeSense; see `host::is_armed_here`. armed_machine string | null optional The team-shared id of the machine whose session server arms this routine: it fires there on the machine's own clock, with or without a desktop. `armed_host` then names the Mac that manages the arm (pushes it, and records its runs); no Mac fires it itself. Old clients carry it as an unknown key. command array optional command[] string optional handover_from object | null optional The machine this routine moved off and the epoch of that move, until that machine acknowledged it stopped firing it. No Mac fires the routine meanwhile (it may still fire there), whichever Mac reads this; the Mac that manages it clears it once acknowledged. handover_from.epoch integer optional handover_from.machine…

entries.title: routine.yml JSON Schema serde field reference
entries.text: A routine saves either an agent task or an argv command. An agent routine lives at config/agents/<agent-id>/routines/<id>/routine.yml ; the path supplies its agent. Command routines live under config/agents/_command/routines/<id>/routine.yml . The table below is generated from RoutineDef and its nested serde models. Open the standalone JSON Schema or schema browser . The schema describes accepted wire shapes; save-time validation also checks schedules, agents, placement, limits and combinations. Flattened fields are preserved. Some are supported runner extensions, including policy.max_wait ; other unknown fields have no guaranteed behavior. Also available: Agent schema and role configuration schema .

entries.title: Policy: spend cap
entries.text: Policy: spend cap A fresh agent routine may set policy.budget_usd , for example {per_day: 10, per_week: 40} . Both fields are optional positive finite USD. Its runs aggregate by routine handle across sessions and machines, and also count toward the agent's own cap. Either scope can refuse a fire with budget_reached . A wake routine must cap its agent instead. Command routines cannot have a cap. Capped routines cannot be armed on a machine, and machine-armed routines cannot add a cap. Read Spend caps before changing a limit.

entries.title: Tool reference
entries.text: Tool reference Reference for the routine tools that read a routine, run-side tools used from inside a routine run, move where a routine fires, and the session wakeup timers. Where a tool takes sessionId , identity comes from the verified MCP connection; a supplied sessionId must name the caller itself, and an unbound caller is refused. Reading routines and results routine_get Reads one routine in full. id comes from routine_list ; optional agent refuses ( validation ) unless the routine belongs to that agent. Returns {status:"ok", data:{id, scope, agent_key, mode, effective_mode, owner, enabled, revision, schedule_in_words, routine, runs}} with this Mac's last 5 runs, plus budgetUsd , budgetPending and spend ( ok , warn , reached or unpriced ). A routine with content_stale was armed on a machine and not refreshed since its agent changed. { "tool": "routine_get", "arguments": { "id": "<id from routine_list>" } } routine_result Reads the last successful private structured result and the latest attempt for a routine. It is a cached read: it never launches an agent, and it reports schema_compatible and the success timestamp explicitly. Returns the snapshot, latest_attempt status, revision and schema_compatible . { "tool": "routine_result", "arguments": { "id": "<id from routine_list>" } } routine_delete Archives any routine you can see: it stops firing and leaves routine_list , and its run history stays readable. Any visible routine is yours to change, a teammate's included; the change is a local edit to the context repo, and sharing it is a git push your agent makes. Notifies no one. Returns {status:"ok", data:{id, archived:true, revision}} . { "tool": "routine_delete", "arguments": { "id": "<id from routine_list>" } } Inside a routine run routine_context When a routine launched you, tells you what you are running and why. sessionId is required and answers for the routine run that session is running; optional runId selects the run named in a wake header. Returns data:{run_id, routine_id, routine_name, revision,…

entries.title: Validate before enabling
entries.text: Validate before enabling routine_create {..., dryRun:true} runs the real create validation without saving. Read the envelope status ; only ok is success. Then read data.warnings , effective_mode , next_fires and the selected agent. Create with enabled:false until ready. Read the saved definition with routine_get ; use routine_update with its latest baseRevision . The schema browser’s validateYaml page bridge is currently unavailable; its local shape check does not establish semantic validity. Use routine_create with events and dryRun:true for shared event validation; see the cookbook .

entries.title: Context in a fresh team run
entries.text: Context in a fresh team run On this Mac, an agent routine targeting team_workspace starts in its own scratch directory for that routine and saved agent, outside shared team content. Before each new session, CodeSense clears that pair's scratch files and prepares the saved agent's current context and startup , including merge-marked workspace files such as team hooks in .claude/settings.json . Both visible and headless sessions receive these files. Save outputs you need to keep through the appropriate content or Notes tools; files left in the routine's working directory are temporary. Reassigning a routine to a different saved agent selects a different directory, preserving the previous agent's live files. Old per-agent directories remain; they are not automatically removed on reassignment. # In the saved agent's agent.yaml: context: - path: skills/evaluate dest: .claude/skills/evaluate # In its routine.yml: mode: fresh task: Run /evaluate, save the result, then call signal_done. where: kind: team_workspace Preview with agent_preview {agent: "org/repo/team/agent", teamWorkspace: true} : its context.files destinations are the context paths prepared in the run's cwd. Changes to skills or the agent's context apply on the next spawn, without restarting the app. Projected files are never written into shared team content. each_mac prepares the directory on each firing Mac; one_mac prepares it only on the armed host. Explicit remote-machine launches continue using their prepared remote repo workspace. On this Mac, a wake delivers only to a live session tagged at launch with that routine's identity. It never adopts another routine's session or an untagged agent started from the Agents tab, even when the agent and cwd match; it launches its own session instead. Remote wakes retain their existing per-agent/workspace matching and admission for now. Delivery leaves the live session's files untouched; an absent agent gets the waking routine's prepared directory before launch. A later fresh spawn for the same routine and saved…

entries.title: Context in a fresh team run
Which one?
entries.text: Which one? You say to the agent It makes With "Add a routine for your session to check the build in 20 minutes" a timer on its session schedule_wakeup in: "20m" "Remind yourself at 3pm to post the summary" a timer schedule_wakeup at "Check the deploy every 10 minutes until it's green" a repeating timer schedule_wakeup every: "10m" "Make a routine for Barb to triage issues every weekday" a routine on Barb, wake routine_create mode: "wake" "Every night, start a new agent that writes the changelog" a routine, start a new routine_create mode: "fresh"

entries.title: Setting one
entries.text: Setting one schedule_wakeup { "sessionId": "$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID", "in": "20m", "name": "Check the build", "prompt": "Check CI for PR #212. Green: merge it. Red: read the failing job and fix it." } // → { timerId, nextAt, name, machineId, sessionId } repeating, with an end { "sessionId": "$CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID", "in": "10m", "every": "10m", "count": 6, "name": "Watch the deploy", "prompt": "Check the deploy. If it is green, say so and cancel this timer with cancel_wakeup." } sessionId is the caller's own session. Another session's id is refused: a timer can only wake the session that set it. Exactly one of in ( 90s , 20m , 2h , 1h30m , 1d ) or at (RFC 3339 with its offset, in the future). every repeats (at least 1m ), with at most one of until or count . list_wakeups lists the session's timers, soonest first; cancel_wakeup stops one. minGap (optional, 30m , 2h ; 1m to 7d ) is the least time between two of its deliveries: a fire inside it folds into the last one. Set it when each fire starts heavy work; a light check needs none. Limits: 10 active timers per session, 200 per machine. No lifetime cap: a session can take hundreds of small wakes over a week. A fixed safety backstop (120 wakes an hour per session, every source together) refuses the rest as rate_limited , posts one inbox note naming the top source, and resumes on its own.

entries.title: Remind yourself.
entries.text: Arc G · Routines Remind yourself. A timer belongs to one session. It comes back to that conversation, then it is gone. Barb · 9:00 schedule_wakeup in 20m Check the build timer · 20m · this tab Barb · 9:20 same conversation, idle sets types [timer: Check the build | fire 1]

entries.title: When it fires
entries.text: When it fires It waits for idle. The prompt is typed only when the agent is idle at its prompt, nobody has typed in the tab for 3 seconds, and no permission prompt is waiting. Fires due while one still waits fold into it. It arrives as a new message , headed [timer: Check the build | fire 1] . The tab's caption says "Woken by Check the build" and the scrollback gets a marker. It ends with the session. Exit, close or crash, and its timers are gone. On a connected machine the machine keeps and fires them, so they keep firing while the desktop is closed; setting, listing and cancelling need the desktop connected. Timers work in any interactive CodeSense session, a saved agent or an unnamed one, on this Mac or a connected machine. They don't work for headless runs, and not yet for Codex.

entries.title: In the app
entries.text: In the app Remind this agent… in a terminal tab's menu sets a timer as you: in 20 minutes, at a time, or every N minutes, with a message. A tab with timers shows a clock in its tab pill and a countdown chip in its caption. The chip's popover lists each timer with Cancel, plus the tab's wake history. Keep this… on a timer turns it into a routine on the tab's agent, with the timer's prompt and schedule filled in. For an unnamed session it saves the session as an agent first.

entries.title: Try this now
entries.text: Try this now Ask the agent in any CodeSense tab: Add a routine for your session to tell me the time in 2 minutes. It calls schedule_wakeup with in: "2m" . Watch the caption chip count down, then the message arrive.

entries.title: How to do this via MCP
entries.text: How to do this via MCP // Set, list, cancel (always your own session) codesense.invoke('schedule_wakeup', { sessionId, in: '20m', name: 'Check the build', prompt: '…' }) codesense.invoke('list_wakeups', { sessionId }) codesense.invoke('cancel_wakeup', { sessionId, timerId })

entries.title: Timer or routine — your session or Barb
entries.text: A timer is a temporary routine for the session you're in. Tell an agent "add a routine for your session to check the build in 20 minutes", and it sets a timer on its own session: later, once it is idle, the timer's prompt arrives in the same conversation, so the agent still knows what it was doing. A timer never starts anything, never reaches another session, is never written to git, and ends when the session ends. Tell it "make a routine for Barb to do X every weekday" instead, and that is a routine : saved under Barb, shared with the team, and firing for as long as it exists, whether or not today's Barb session is still open.

entries.title: Routines live with their agent.
entries.text: Arc G · Routines Routines live with their agent. Every routine runs an agent, so every routine lives under one. routine · in git owned by a saved agent; survives everything <team>/config/agents/manager/ ├── agent.yaml └── routines/ ├── manager-wake/routine.yml └── manager-ensure/routine.yml no agent: key — the folder says whose timer · not a file owned by one running session schedule_wakeup kept by the machine that runs the session ends with the session Routines are shared with the team by git. Timers are never written anywhere.

entries.title: On-disk layout
entries.text: On-disk layout <team>/config/agents/ ├── manager/ │ ├── agent.yaml │ └── routines/ │ ├── manager-wake/ │ │ ├── routine.yml # the current definition │ │ └── revisions/1.yml # its own history, separate from the agent's │ └── manager-ensure/ │ └── routine.yml ├── _builtin/ │ └── claude/ routines/ # routines on a built-in starter (fresh only) └── _unassigned/ routines/ # a routine whose agent is missing: "Pick an agent" _personal/<account>/<org>/_scratch/agents/<org>~<team>~<agent>/routines/<id>/ # your Only me routine on a team agent

entries.title: Ids, starters and the old folder
entries.text: Ids, starters and the old folder Ids are team-unique A routine id is unique across the whole team, whichever agent holds it, so <org>/<team>/<id> always names one routine and its run history. Moving a routine to another agent keeps its id and its runs. The folder name is the id . Agent folders starting with _ are never agents. agent_get lists an agent's routines; routine_list takes an agent filter. The old config/routines/ Routines used to live in config/routines/<id>/ and name their agent. CodeSense copies each one forward under its agent the first time it loads the team, with mode: fresh written so it behaves as before, and leaves the old file as a pointer for one release. Nothing new is written there. Copy, never move: an old client's edit is carried forward. An id clash is renamed, with a visible note. The read-only CodeSense docs ship in the new layout already.

entries.title: How CodeSense finds them
entries.text: How CodeSense finds them For each team you can see, it reads every config/agents/*/routines/*/routine.yml (starters and _unassigned included), plus any old config/routines/ entry not yet carried forward. A file that doesn't parse, or whose id doesn't match its folder, is skipped (logged, never fires) and doesn't show up. A routine you write by hand is only fully checked when it is saved through CodeSense, so check it first with routine_create dryRun: true . Enabled routines are armed on the Mac that runs them ( armed_here ). A routine that runs on each Mac is armed on every Mac whose user turned it on.

entries.title: Files next to a routine
entries.text: Files next to a routine A routine's folder holds its routine.yml and its revisions/ . Keep anything else the task needs (a prompt partial, a checklist) under content/ , where the agent reads it like any other file and it versions with the team. State a run produces belongs in the run's result ( signal_done , routine_done or routine_publish_result ), which the next run reads back.

entries.title: Try this now
entries.text: Try this now List the Manager's routines in your editable context repo.

entries.title: How to do this via MCP
entries.text: How to do this via MCP // Every routine you can see, or one agent's codesense.invoke('routine_list', {}) codesense.invoke('routine_list', { agent: 'manager' }) // An agent and its routines in one read codesense.invoke('agent_get', { id: 'manager' }) // Create one under its agent (checks and writes nothing with dryRun) codesense.invoke('routine_create', { name: 'Morning triage', agent: 'barb', mode: 'wake', when: 'weekdays 09:00', task: '…', dryRun: true, })

entries.title: Why routines belong to agents
entries.text: Every routine starts or wakes an agent, so a routine belongs to that agent. Its file sits under the agent's folder, config/agents/<agent>/routines/<id>/routine.yml , and the path names the agent: the YAML has no agent: key. In the app the agent's Routines section in the Agents tab lists them, and Agents | Schedule shows every agent's upcoming fires. Archiving an agent archives its routines (after a confirm that lists them); unarchiving it offers to bring them back. A timer is the other kind: a temporary routine owned by one running session. It is never a file. It lives with the machine running that session and ends when the session ends.

entries.title: Worked example — a wake task with a no-op branch
entries.text: Worked example — a wake task with a no-op branch The seeded manager-ensure routine wakes the Manager every hour. Its task is written to the Manager itself — it is typed into the Manager's session — and every branch ends quietly. If no Manager is running, the same text starts one. mode: wake task: | Check the manager queue. Call role_state with role "manager". If anything is pending, claim it with claim_role_messages and carry on with /manage-team. If nothing is pending, say "manager queue empty" in one line and wait.

entries.title: Exit contract
entries.text: Exit contract routine_done (wake) A woken session gets the task headed [routine: <name> | run <id>] . It calls routine_done with that run id, an outcome and a summary: the run ends, the session keeps working. Without it the run is recorded delivered . Never signal_done for a wake: that ends the session's whole task. signal_done (start a new) The agent calls signal_done with a one-line summary. The engine logs the run as ok and tears the session down. The routines console shows the summary; the next trigger fires on its own timeline. no-op "Nothing to do" is a valid outcome. The agent still calls signal_done with a short rationale ("manager queue empty"). A tick that fires and signals no-op is cheap and leaves a scannable breadcrumb in run history. timeout If the agent exceeds policy.max_runtime , the engine kills the session and logs the run as timeout . The routines console shows the partial transcript. Fix: shorten the task, tighten the MCP calls, or raise max_runtime . overlap: skip With policy.overlap: skip , a tick that fires while the previous run is still in flight is logged as skipped and does nothing. Use this for idempotent cron routines where overlap would mean duplicate work. fail An unhandled error inside the agent's runtime (crash, bridge rejection) is logged as fail with a short reason. The next scheduled tick fires normally; CodeSense doesn't back off automatically.

entries.title: Tasks.
entries.text: Arc G · Routines Tasks. A task is a prompt template, a context substitution, and an exit contract. 1 · trigger fires with context 2 · substitute {{trigger.*}} 3 · session agent spawns 4 · work MCP calls 5 · exit signal_done The agent decides when it's done. The engine kills on policy.max_runtime. Stdout / tool-call history is captured and surfaced on the routines console.

entries.title: Task shape
entries.text: Task shape Template body — a markdown block (YAML's | literal) that reads like a short memo. State the trigger, enumerate the steps, name the signal_done payload. Keep it under ~40 lines; longer tasks drift. Trigger-context placeholders — anywhere the body says {{trigger.X}} , a fresh run substitutes the matching field on the trigger event (table below). Unknown keys stay literal — the agent will mention them in its reply and you'll notice. A wake fills in only {{date}} and {{timestamp}} : the text is typed into a live session, so it carries no run-specific data. MCP calls — the agent works via its allowlisted MCP servers (declared in its agent.yaml ). The seeded tasks lean on read_messages , claim_role_messages , role_state and routine_done . A task never wakes another agent with send_to_session : give that agent its own wake routine. Scope — the task body never names the context repo path explicitly; the engine spawns the session with the right where and the agent uses its MCP tools against that scope. Portable across workspaces for free.

entries.title: Try this now
entries.text: Try this now Check a routine without saving it: routine_create with dryRun: true validates the schedule, the agent and the mode, and reports warnings such as a /command the agent doesn't start with.

entries.title: How to do this via MCP
entries.text: How to do this via MCP // Check without writing codesense.invoke('routine_create', { name: '…', agent: 'manager', mode: 'wake', task: '…', dryRun: true }) // Live fire codesense.invoke('routine_run_now', { id: 'manager-wake' }) // Inside a woken session: finish this run, keep the session codesense.invoke('routine_done', { sessionId, runId, outcome: 'success', summary: '…' }) // Tail the run (routines-console does this live) codesense.subscribeContext({ topic: 'routines.runs', id: 'manager-wake' }, (ev) => { … })

entries.title: What a task is
entries.text: The task: block is the prompt the agent session receives on each fire. It's a short, well-structured instruction — not a program. The engine substitutes {{trigger.*}} placeholders, hands the resulting text to the agent as its opening message, and watches for the agent to call signal_done . There are no return values and no RPC — the agent's observable effects are the MCP calls it makes and the files it writes.

entries.title: Worked example — a wake task with a no-op branch
Agent follows the command · after
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Trigger cookbook: schedule, metadata trigger, events and chaining
entries.text: Agent follows the command · after Create the predecessor review-command from the command chain before this dry run. A successful predecessor run fires this agent routine with {{trigger.result_text}} . on: finished continues after succeeded , failed , timed_out , needs_you or ended ; cancelled does not fire a chain. Trigger the upstream command after enabling both; compare the downstream trigger run_id to the upstream run. Dry-run success establishes the saved dependency, not a completed chain. MCP: routine_create dry run { "agent": "default", "mode": "fresh", "maxRuntime": "5m", "enabled": false, "dryRun": true, "id": "review-agent", "name": "Agent follows the command", "task": "The upstream result names the changed story: {{trigger.result_text}}. Open that path, review the story and report your findings.", "after": { "routine": "review-command", "on": "succeeded" } } Complete routine.yml id: "review-agent" name: "Agent follows the command" owner: "codesense" where: kind: "team_workspace" policy: max_runtime: "5m" revision: 1 agent: "default" mode: "fresh" task: "The upstream result names the changed story: {{trigger.result_text}}. Open that path, review the story and report your findings." after: routine: "review-command" on: "succeeded"

entries.title: Agent finishes · agent_done
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Trigger cookbook: schedule, metadata trigger, events and chaining
entries.text: Agent finishes · agent_done from_agent filters to the saved agent named default; omit it to watch all agents in reach. After enabling, finish a disposable run of that agent and inspect the trigger’s agent, status and summary. This observes an agent completion; use after to watch a specific routine outcome. MCP: routine_create dry run { "agent": "default", "mode": "fresh", "maxRuntime": "5m", "enabled": false, "dryRun": true, "id": "agent-done", "name": "Agent finishes", "task": "Inspect the completion of {{trigger.agent}}: {{trigger.status}} / {{trigger.summary}}. Review the result and report findings.", "events": [ { "kind": "agent_done", "from_agent": "default" } ] } Complete routine.yml id: "agent-done" name: "Agent finishes" owner: "codesense" where: kind: "team_workspace" policy: max_runtime: "5m" revision: 1 agent: "default" mode: "fresh" task: "Inspect the completion of {{trigger.agent}}: {{trigger.status}} / {{trigger.summary}}. Review the result and report findings." triggers: - event: kind: "agent_done" from_agent: "default"

entries.title: Create or update event triggers
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Trigger cookbook: schedule, metadata trigger, events and chaining
entries.text: Create or update event triggers routine_create and routine_update accept events for inbox_idle , agent_done and role_pending , with the same validation as handwritten YAML. Each item becomes triggers: [{event: ...}] ; use metadataTriggers for metadata changes. from_agent is valid only for agent_done ; omit it for all agents in reach. It is an agent id or full key, without an existence check. On update, omitted or null events preserves existing event triggers; [] clears these three kinds; a nonempty list replaces only them. Schedules and metadata triggers remain. A refusal returns status: validation with an indexed field such as events[1].role and a hint; nothing is saved. Creation alone supports dryRun:true : inspect the resolved data.triggers , then save and enable deliberately. There is no update dry run. These three event kinds support each_mac ; metadata triggers still require one_mac . Local event triggers cannot be armed on a remote machine. The complete YAML blocks omit machine-owned placement. If installing by hand, keep the routine disabled, open the app editor, make a harmless edit (such as the name), then choose Save changes to validate it. Use routine_arm_on {id, machine:"this_mac"} before enabling a one_mac routine. The schema browser’s local shape check does not establish semantic validity.

entries.title: Unread mail at an idle prompt · inbox_idle
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Trigger cookbook: schedule, metadata trigger, events and chaining
entries.text: Unread mail at an idle prompt · inbox_idle With this fresh-mode example, idle sessions with unread mail in reach of the team fire it; {{trigger.sessions}} identifies them. For a wake routine, only the owning agent’s own session with unread mail fires and receives it. To test, send ordinary inbox mail to an idle disposable agent session, then inspect the run. After three wakes that leave the same mail unread, the runner stops repeating that mail and records the reason in routine run history. Use routine_runs then routine_run to inspect it; write the task to read the mail. MCP: routine_create dry run { "agent": "default", "mode": "fresh", "maxRuntime": "5m", "enabled": false, "dryRun": true, "id": "inbox-idle", "name": "Unread mail at an idle prompt", "task": "Inspect the idle sessions {{trigger.sessions}} and read their pending inbox messages. Report any work needing attention.", "events": [ { "kind": "inbox_idle" } ] } Complete routine.yml id: "inbox-idle" name: "Unread mail at an idle prompt" owner: "codesense" where: kind: "team_workspace" policy: max_runtime: "5m" revision: 1 agent: "default" mode: "fresh" task: "Inspect the idle sessions {{trigger.sessions}} and read their pending inbox messages. Report any work needing attention." triggers: - event: kind: "inbox_idle"

entries.title: Story moves to review · metadata_change
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Trigger cookbook: schedule, metadata trigger, events and chaining
entries.text: Story moves to review · metadata_change A metadata trigger watches story status entering review from in-progress. Selection uses the same query model as query_context ; target and previous currently use op: eq . Omit previous for any transition into the target value. First discovery and app restart baseline existing matches; they do not replay them. Enable before making a new transition, keep runs_on: one_mac , then inspect the run trigger to identify the document. The dry run validates the condition, not an observed transition. MCP: routine_create dry run { "agent": "default", "mode": "fresh", "maxRuntime": "5m", "enabled": false, "dryRun": true, "id": "story-review", "name": "Story moves to review", "task": "Review the relevant stories and report the result.", "metadataTriggers": [ { "selection": { "where": { "kinds": [ "story" ] } }, "target": { "key": "status", "op": "eq", "value": "review" }, "previous": { "key": "status", "op": "eq", "value": "in-progress" } } ] } Complete routine.yml id: "story-review" name: "Story moves to review" owner: "codesense" where: kind: "team_workspace" policy: max_runtime: "5m" revision: 1 agent: "default" mode: "fresh" task: "Review the relevant stories and report the result." triggers: - event: kind: "metadata_change" metadata: selection: where: kinds: - "story" target: key: "status" op: "eq" value: "review" previous: key: "status" op: "eq" value: "in-progress"

entries.title: Read a controlled run
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Trigger cookbook: schedule, metadata trigger, events and chaining
entries.text: Read a controlled run After enabling, induce the real event in a disposable story or message thread. Use routine_runs {id} and routine_run {runId} to inspect the outcome, trigger and summary. Agent fresh runs finish through signal_done or process exit; wake runs use routine_done . Commands succeed on exit 0 and fail on a nonzero exit. A dry run proves authoring validation; it does not prove your external command, clock or agent instructions work live.

entries.title: Role mail arrives · role_pending
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Trigger cookbook: schedule, metadata trigger, events and chaining
entries.text: Role mail arrives · role_pending Use {kind:"role_pending"} when a dispatcher needs every role queue in reach. Use {kind:"role_pending",role:"reviewer"} when this routine should run only for reviewer mail. The example below uses that filter; omit role for the wildcard. A team routine watches its own team; a private routine watches teams in its org. Empty or whitespace-only role names fail validation; role names need no registry entry. The run receives {{trigger.role}} , {{trigger.message_id}} , {{trigger.org}} and {{trigger.team}} . Notification does not claim mail: use register_role , claim_role_messages , accept_role_message before work and ack_role_message after work. After enabling, enqueue a disposable message with send_role_message , then inspect both role_state and the routine run. A defaultHandler is configuration only and does not automatically launch an agent. MCP: routine_create dry run { "agent": "default", "mode": "fresh", "maxRuntime": "5m", "enabled": false, "dryRun": true, "id": "role-pending", "name": "Role mail arrives", "task": "Call role_state for the reviewer queue. If it has pending work, register_role for reviewer, then claim_role_messages. Before doing the work, call accept_role_message with disposition kind work; after finishing, call ack_role_message with its receiptId and the claim details. If an existingReceipt is returned, finish that accepted work and acknowledge its receipt instead of accepting again. Ignore other queues.", "events": [ { "kind": "role_pending", "role": "reviewer" } ] } Complete routine.yml id: "role-pending" name: "Role mail arrives" owner: "codesense" where: kind: "team_workspace" policy: max_runtime: "5m" revision: 1 agent: "default" mode: "fresh" task: "Call role_state for the reviewer queue. If it has pending work, register_role for reviewer, then claim_role_messages. Before doing the work, call accept_role_message with disposition kind work; after finishing, call ack_role_message with its receiptId and the claim details. If an existingReceipt is returned,…

entries.title: Weekday review · schedule
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Trigger cookbook: schedule, metadata trigger, events and chaining
entries.text: Weekday review · schedule Runs weekdays at 09:00 UTC. The disabled draft has an empty data.next_fires ; check its schedule wording, then enable and verify the next three weekday fires in that zone. Schedules use five-field cron and may not fire more often than every five minutes. After saving and enabling, wait for the next listed fire, then inspect its run. MCP: routine_create dry run { "agent": "default", "mode": "fresh", "maxRuntime": "5m", "enabled": false, "dryRun": true, "id": "morning-review", "name": "Weekday review", "task": "Review the relevant stories and report the result.", "when": "weekdays 09:00", "tz": "UTC" } Complete routine.yml id: "morning-review" name: "Weekday review" owner: "codesense" where: kind: "team_workspace" policy: max_runtime: "5m" revision: 1 agent: "default" mode: "fresh" task: "Review the relevant stories and report the result." triggers: - schedule: cron: "0 9 * * 1-5" tz: "UTC"

entries.title: metadata trigger routine_create dryRun cookbook
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Trigger cookbook: schedule, metadata trigger, events and chaining
entries.text: Choose one trigger, preview it, then enable it deliberately. Each card has the actual routine_create arguments and the equivalent complete YAML. These examples share machine-readable inputs with the routine-create seam tests. First save an agent whose id is default , or substitute your saved agent id in the MCP form and YAML path. Agent routines go under config/agents/default/routines/<id>/routine.yml . A command routine goes under config/agents/_command/routines/<id>/routine.yml . Examples start disabled. A dry run reports a plan; it never fires the trigger. For each MCP block call routine_create with that JSON. Require status: ok and data.dry_run: true ; inspect warnings, effective mode, selected agent and next fires. A refusal explains the invalid field. To save, change dryRun to false. Use routine_get to read back the definition. Trigger a controlled test before enabling unattended operation.

entries.title: Copyable trigger recipes

See command routines for the metadata → command → agent chain. For role_pending, omit role to watch every queue in reach, or set role:"reviewer" to watch just reviewer mail.

entries.title: Pick your trigger.
entries.text: Arc G · Routines Pick your trigger. Same routine shape. Different reasons to fire it. inbox_idle queue goes quiet cron wall-clock tick manual human clicks run agent_done another agent finished each_mac scope modifier routine.yml triggers → task → session wakes or starts its agent No central scheduler. Each trigger is a separate reason the engine lets the clock tick through.

entries.title: 4 · agent_done
entries.text: 4 · agent_done event · agent_done Review after the Builder finishes When: an agent finishes ( signal_done ); from_agent narrows it to one. Why: to chain agents without a dispatcher. The routine shows under the agent it runs (the Reviewer), with an "after amelia-builder" note. Trigger context (fresh runs only): {{trigger.session_id}} , {{trigger.status}} , {{trigger.summary}} , {{trigger.agent}} . # config/agents/winston-reviewer/routines/review-after-build/routine.yml id: review-after-build name: Review what the Builder shipped owner: you mode: fresh task: | The Builder finished: {{trigger.status}} — {{trigger.summary}}. If it opened a PR, review it with bmad-code-review and post the review. Call signal_done with the verdict. where: kind: team_workspace triggers: - event: kind: agent_done from_agent: amelia-builder policy: max_runtime: 30m revision: 1

entries.title: 2 · cron
entries.text: 2 · cron schedule · cron Keep a manager on the queue When: on a wall-clock cadence: a 5-field cron in an IANA zone ( tz ); nothing more often than every 5 minutes. Why: for liveness backstops, synthesis passes, nightly sweeps. As a wake on machine: any , this one checks in with the Manager wherever it runs, and starts one when none is running. A Manager on a machine that is offline still counts as running: that fire is undelivered (machine_offline) and no second Manager starts while that machine stays offline. Choose limits for the work: a light check like this one can wake every 15 minutes for weeks; there is no lifetime cap. A wake that starts heavy work should set min_gap (and maybe max_wakes_per_day or max_wakes ) under policy , so it never rewakes or piles up. # config/agents/manager/routines/manager-ensure/routine.yml id: manager-ensure name: Keep a manager on the queue owner: codesense mode: wake task: | Check the manager queue. Call role_state with role "manager". If anything is pending, claim it with claim_role_messages and carry on with /manage-team. If nothing is pending, say "manager queue empty" in one line and wait. where: kind: team_workspace machine: any triggers: - schedule: cron: "0 * * * *" tz: UTC policy: max_runtime: 5m overlap: skip revision: 1

entries.title: 6 · each_mac
entries.text: 6 · each_mac runs_on · each_mac One per teammate's Mac When: paired with any trigger above as a scope. Why: sessions and inboxes are per Mac, so a recipe each teammate turns on for their own Mac ("Run on my Mac", or routine_set_enabled ) wakes or starts that Mac's own agent. So an each_mac routine must use machine: local (or leave it out), except that a fresh one may use any (each Mac starts its own); a machine id is refused in either mode, since every teammate's Mac would wake or start the same agent there. # config/agents/winston-reviewer/routines/reviewer-wake/routine.yml id: reviewer-wake name: Wake the reviewer owner: you mode: wake task: | You have unread mail. Claim one message for the reviewer role with claim_role_messages, review it with bmad-code-review, then ack it. where: kind: team_workspace machine: local triggers: - event: kind: inbox_idle policy: max_runtime: 30m runs_on: each_mac revision: 1

entries.title: 1 · inbox_idle
entries.text: 1 · inbox_idle event · inbox_idle Wake the agent when mail waits When: a session sits idle at its prompt with unread mail (at most once every 30 seconds per routine). With mode: wake only the routine's own agent's sessions count, and the one with the mail is woken: a worker's mail never wakes the Manager. With mode: fresh any session launched in the team counts. Why: a Claude agent with an inbox waiter is woken by new mail at once, but one that leaves its mail unread, or an agent with no waiter, sits idle with it; this is the nudge for those. After 3 wakes that leave the same mail unread, the runner stops repeating that mail and records the reason in routine run history. Inspect it with routine_runs then routine_run . Trigger context (fresh runs only): {{trigger.sessions}} , {{trigger.count}} . # config/agents/manager/routines/manager-wake/routine.yml id: manager-wake name: Wake the manager owner: codesense mode: wake task: | You have unread mail. Call read_messages with your session id, then claim_role_messages for the manager role, and carry on with /manage-team. If there is nothing for you, say so in one line and wait. where: kind: team_workspace machine: local triggers: - event: kind: inbox_idle policy: max_runtime: 5m runs_on: each_mac revision: 1

entries.title: 3 · manual
entries.text: 3 · manual manual Human-gated release cut When: only when someone presses Run now on the routine, a dashboard's Refresh calls routineRefresh , or an agent calls routine_run_now . Why: for operations you keep in human hands — a release cut, a destructive sweep, an expensive one-shot. No triggers: at all. # config/agents/amelia-builder/routines/ship-release/routine.yml id: ship-release name: Cut a release owner: you mode: fresh task: | Confirm main is green, cut the release, and tag the merge commit. Call signal_done with the tag name. where: kind: team_workspace policy: max_runtime: 30m visible: true revision: 1

entries.title: When a field changes
entries.text: When a field changes In the routine editor, add a metadata trigger, choose a document kind and optional folder, then a field and the value it changes to. For example: when a story's status becomes in-progress. Set From to planning to require that exact transition. Custom frontmatter and HTML cs:* fields use the same selection and equality as query_context . List fields say “gains”: gaining blocked in tags fires once. With routine_create , set when: "" for triggers without a schedule: {"metadataTriggers":[{ "selection":{"where":{"kinds":["story"],"pathPrefix":"stories/"}}, "target":{"key":"status","op":"eq","value":"in-progress"} }]} For planning → in-progress, add "previous":{"key":"status","op":"eq","value":"planning"} beside target. A custom boolean target can be {"key":"review_requested","op":"eq","value":true} . Text compares exactly; a JSON number compares numerically. The editor sends text. routine_get returns the conditions. On update, omit metadataTriggers to preserve them, send the whole replacement list to edit, or send [] to remove them. Schedules and other events remain. First discovery, restart, enabling and editing establish a baseline: documents already matching do not replay. Only a later observed entry fires. Unrelated edits do not fire; leaving and re-entering can. New or moved files without an observed previous value do not fire. Debounced saves may settle into one change; changes while observation was stopped are not replayed. The routine watches its synced team or personal files even with another team displayed. Normal overlap and placement policies apply, without the agent-done five-minute throttle. Wake prompts stay static. Read routine_context with your sessionId and the wake header's runId : trigger_payload identifies org, team, path, story ID, field, previous_present, previous_value and new_value; coalesced_payloads retains every merged change. Fresh tasks may also use supported {{trigger.*}} fields.

entries.title: 5 · role_pending
entries.text: 5 · role_pending event · role_pending Start a builder for each queued task When: a message is queued for a role inbox the routine can reach (its own team's for a team routine; every team in the org for an Only me one). It watches the builder queue in this example. Omit role for every queue in reach. It fires once per message, and never on a message its own run queued. Why: nothing claims a role message on its own; this lets a routine start an agent that claims it. Trigger context: {{trigger.role}} , {{trigger.message_id}} , {{trigger.org}} , {{trigger.team}} . # config/agents/amelia-builder/routines/build-on-request/routine.yml id: build-on-request name: Build what lands in the builder queue owner: you mode: fresh task: | A message is waiting for the {{trigger.role}} role. Claim it with claim_role_messages, do the work it asks for, then call signal_done. where: kind: team_workspace triggers: - event: kind: role_pending role: builder policy: max_runtime: 60m revision: 1
