entries.text: How to do this via MCP // Every routine you can see (each says its triggers in words) routine_list {} // Fire a routine right now, through its own overlap rule routine_run_now { id: 'manager-wake' } // Its recent runs routine_runs { id: 'manager-wake' }

entries.title: How triggers compose
entries.text: A routine's triggers: list says when it fires; with none it is manual only. Each entry is a schedule (cron and time zone) or an event of kind inbox_idle , role_pending , agent_done or metadata_change . You can list several in one routine — "fire on inbox_idle, and also every hour as a safety net." Whatever fires it, the routine's mode decides what happens: wake types the task into its agent's running session, start a new ( fresh ) starts a new one. runs_on: each_mac is not a trigger but a scope for per-Mac recipes. Metadata triggers run personally or once for the team. Each example below is a drop-into-your-repo copy, under the agent it runs.

entries.title: event · agent_done Review after the Builder finishes
event · inbox_idle Wake the agent when mail waits
event · role_pending Start a builder for each queued task
runs_on · each_mac One per teammate's Mac
schedule · cron Keep a manager on the queue
Why was a fire skipped with budget_reached?
entries.text: Why was a fire skipped with budget_reached? The routine or its agent has reached a daily or weekly spend cap, or has usage that cannot be priced. The skipped run names the scope, window, spend and cap; an unpriced refusal names the model. Open the agent's Overview → Spend cap , or the fresh routine's cap block. Wait for the local window to roll over, or have a person save or accept a cap. Changing a file or MCP value upward leaves the raise pending. While a local agent is held, mail remains in its inbox and a person can still type. The current turn finishes; queued automatic turns wait. See Spend caps .

entries.title: Where to look first
entries.text: The routines console is the one surface that answers every question on the ladder above — the next scheduled fire, the last run with its status chip, the recent-N timeline, and the per-run detail with task template, stdout, and the publish side-channel. Open it first; the symptom names the step that failed.

entries.title: When a routine misbehaves.
entries.text: Arc G · Routines When a routine misbehaves. Six questions, walked top to bottom. The first "no" is the fault. 1 · Is the scheduler running? — routines console shows a next-fire 2 · Did the trigger evaluate true? — cron matched; inbox idle 3 · Is armed_here true for this Mac? 4 · Did the agent launch? — agent exists, permissions ok 5 · Did the task finish? — signal_done or exit before maxRuntime 6 · Was the result published? — routine_publish_result + schema_compatible

entries.title: Symptom catalogue
entries.text: Symptom catalogue A run is stuck in running step 5 The agent launched but never called signal_done and never exited. maxRuntime will cut it eventually; you can cancel sooner. Open the run on the routines console; the stdout tail usually names the last thing it did. Use the MCP tool routine_cancel {runId} , with a run_id from routine_runs . It cancels one queued or running run. A fresh run's agent or command stops; a wake run keeps its existing session alive. See the cancel example for returned state, authorization and wake withdrawal errors. To stop future starts too, call routine_set_enabled {id, enabled:false} . Fix the task: either add an explicit signal_done step, or lower policy.max_runtime so stuck sessions fail fast and surface loudly. OpenCode agents. When the model provider answers with a server error (5xx), OpenCode retries without printing anything and without exiting, so only policy.max_runtime ends the run. For OpenCode, set a short one ( 30m suggested). A headless OpenCode run denies any tool outside read-only tools and CodeSense's own unless the agent's permissions.opencode allows it; a denied tool continues with an error turn instead of stopping the run. A headless OpenCode run that exits without calling signal_done ends with the model's final text as its summary; that text is a summary, never the run's result. A provider rejection (a 4xx, an unknown model) fails the run with its message. Unattended OpenCode. The OpenCode unattended starter keeps --auto . Escalating agents ( --auto or an all-allow map) get an allow base headless, and their own denies still apply, so a bash: deny stays denied. Pair such an agent with a sandbox, and still give each of its routines a short policy.max_runtime ( 30m suggested). Scheduled fires are missed step 1 · 3 A cron routine shows no run at the expected time. Three usual causes. Mac was asleep. Local Macs skip fires while asleep (standard Mac behavior). The routines console shows the skipped fire with reason mac_asleep . Move must-fire routines to the always-on…

entries.title: Debug toolkit (in order of use)
entries.text: Debug toolkit (in order of use) Tool What it tells you When to reach for it routines console Next fire, last fire, recent-N strip, run detail (task + stdout + publish). Always first. Nine times out of ten the answer is on the strip. routine_runs({ id, limit: 20 }) History with skipped and coalesced fires + reasons. When a schedule looks "quiet" and you want proof of why. routine_run_now({ id }) Fires once through the overlap rule; returns outcome. To bisect: does it work when I fire it by hand? routine_run({ runId }) One run in full: status, delivery reason, result. When a wake says undelivered or unknown and you want the detail. routine_create { …, dryRun: true } Validator error with field + rule. When the console says "load failed" with no detail. routine_cancel({ runId }) Cancels one queued or running run; returns its resulting state. A finished run is unchanged with a validation message. When a run is in running past expected duration. subscribeContext({ topic: 'routines.runs' }, cb) Live stream of fire → done events for the active team. When you want to watch an inbox-idle wake live.

entries.title: Try this now
entries.text: Try this now Open the routines console. The symptom catalogue above maps directly to the surfaces on the page: the strip answers the "did it fire" questions, the run detail answers the "what happened" questions.

entries.title: How to do this via MCP
entries.text: How to do this via MCP // A specific routine's recent history, skipped fires included routine_runs {"id":"acme/api/backend/builder-wake","limit":20} // One run in full (a wake's delivery status and reason included) routine_run {"runId":"<run_id from routine_runs>"} // Fire once by hand; returns outcome: queued / coalesced / skipped:<reason> routine_run_now {"id":"acme/api/backend/builder-wake"} // Cancel one run; future fires stay enabled routine_cancel {"runId":"<run_id from routine_runs>"} These are MCP calls, available from a verified CodeSense connection. In a pane, codesense.routineCancel({key}) cancels this principal's live structured results for a routine, rather than one run by id. To validate a routine, call routine_create with dryRun: true .

entries.title: A hand-written routine never shows up step 0
A run is stuck in running step 5
A session timer didn't fire step 4
A wake says queued, undelivered or unknown step 4
Remote routines fire on the wrong Mac step 3
Why was a fire skipped with budget_reached?
Three contracts you must honor
entries.text: Three contracts you must honor Schema pinning. The resultSchema on the routine must match the payload the task publishes. When you update the schema, bump the routine's revision ; stale clients get schema_compatible: false back from routineResult and must say so, not render stale data as current. Page load never launches. routineResult and routineStatus read the cache. Only an explicit user action (a Refresh button, an on-demand workflow) may call routineRefresh . The validator warns on dashboards that call routineRefresh at the top level. Keep output small. The schema limit is 32 KiB; the payload limit is 1 MiB. Collect once, pre-aggregate, and let the dashboard do presentation. If you need large data, write it under content/ and point the snapshot at a file path.

entries.title: Worked example — DEMO sprint digest
entries.text: Worked example — DEMO sprint digest A cron routine sweeps DEMO's stories every 15 minutes, counts stories by phase, and publishes a tiny structured snapshot. The sprint-digest dashboard reads it and shows the four phase chips with the counts live. No polling in the pane, no HTTP from the pane, and no agent launch on every page open — the snapshot is already there. config/agents/amelia-analyst/routines/sprint-digest/routine.yml id: sprint-digest name: DEMO sprint digest owner: codesense mode: fresh runs_on: one_mac where: kind: team_workspace triggers: - schedule: cron: "*/15 * * * *" tz: UTC policy: max_runtime: 2m result_schema: type: object required: [generated_at, phases] properties: generated_at: { type: string, format: date-time } phases: type: array items: type: object required: [name, count] properties: name: { type: string } count: { type: integer, minimum: 0 } task: | 1. Call query_context with { stories: { epic: "DEMO" } }. 2. Group by phase (plan | design | build | ship); count each. 3. Build the payload matching resultSchema. 4. Call routine_publish_result with { sessionId, payload }. 5. Call signal_done with "ok — N stories across 4 phases". revision: 1 content/sprint-digest.html (excerpt) <script type="module"> const key = { id: "sprint-digest" }; // Load on open — reads the cache, never launches the agent. async function paint() { const { snapshot, latest_attempt, schema_compatible } = await codesense.routineResult(key); if (!snapshot || !schema_compatible) { return render({ status: latest_attempt?.status ?? "collecting" }); } render(snapshot.payload); } // Live update when the routine fires. codesense.onRoutineResult(key, paint); // The Refresh button — the ONLY place the pane may launch the agent. document .querySelector("#refresh") .addEventListener("click", () => codesense.routineRefresh(key)); paint(); </script>

entries.title: Routines that write dashboards.
entries.text: Arc G · Routines Routines that write dashboards. Routine collects. Context repo stores. Dashboard renders live. sprint-digest cron · every 15m routine_publish_result last-good snapshot routine_result cache schema-pinned sprint-digest.html routineResult + onRoutineResult reactive, zero poll publishes reads · notifies The dashboard never launches the agent. The routine owns the fire; the pane just reads.

entries.title: Local vs remote
entries.text: Local vs remote Local. The routine fires on the Mac that owns the team workspace; the snapshot is cached in that Mac's CodeSense state. The dashboard pane renders in your window and reads directly. Remote. If the routine owns a remote context, it fires in the remote account's terminal server. The dashboard reads through the same window.codesense contract — the snapshot is streamed over the bridge exactly as a local snapshot would be. See the Local ⇄ Remote parity matrix for the Run a routine row.

entries.title: Three shapes a dashboard-writing routine can take
entries.text: Three shapes a dashboard-writing routine can take Cron sweep The routine fires on a schedule ( every 15m , hourly , daily 09:00 ). The dashboard reads the last-good snapshot on open and re-reads on onRoutineResult . Great for digests, backlog counts, and any page where "fresh enough" is minutes. Manual-only Omit when ; the routine fires only on routine_run_now or a Refresh button on the pane. Use for expensive collections, or for pages a user opens on demand. Event-driven An agent_done or inbox_idle trigger refreshes the snapshot exactly when upstream data changes. Example: a reviewer's agent_done retriggers the PR-queue digest.

entries.title: How to do this via MCP
entries.text: How to do this via MCP // The dashboard reads (never launches the agent) codesense.routineResult({ id: 'sprint-digest' }) codesense.routineStatus({ id: 'sprint-digest' }) // Only an explicit user action may trigger this codesense.routineRefresh({ id: 'sprint-digest' }) // Live notifications when the routine publishes a new snapshot codesense.onRoutineResult({ id: 'sprint-digest' }, (ev) => { … }) // Inside the routine's agent (the publisher side) codesense.invoke('routine_publish_result', { sessionId, payload }) See mcp-explorer for the full catalog of routine_* tools.

entries.title: Why — reactive dashboards without polling
entries.text: You've got a dashboard that needs data the app doesn't know about — a sprint digest, a PR queue, a per-repo failure rate. You don't want the pane to shell out every time it renders, and you don't want the user clicking Refresh for a stale pane. You want a routine to collect once, publish a structured result, and let every open dashboard pane read the same snapshot. That's the structured-data pattern: a routine with a resultSchema , a dashboard that binds routineResult and onRoutineResult , and a context-repo snapshot as the handoff.

entries.title: What this phase is for
entries.text: What this phase is for A good story graph is the difference between an epic that ships in a week and one that drags for a month. John runs bmad-create-epics-and-stories to slice the design into shippable units and wire their depends_on lists. That skill comes from BMAD, installed in your own repo; CodeSense doesn't ship it. A story is a Markdown file with type: story (or bug , spike ) in its frontmatter, or an HTML page with <meta name="cs:type" content="story"> . The fields CodeSense acts on are story_id , status , source_repo (one of the team's configured repos), depends_on (a list of bare story ids) and supporting_docs . Any other key, such as sprint or parent_epic , is kept as metadata you can query with query_context . The summary is the first ## Purpose or ## Story section. Read the shipped DEMO stories for the shape. Before handing a story on, have the agent call validate_story . It returns findings such as MISSING_SOURCE_REPO , UNPARSEABLE_FRONTMATTER or DUPLICATE_STORY_ID . The same findings show in the metadata band when you open a story, and in the New story form as you type.

entries.text: What this phase is for A sprint plan says what the team is doing this cycle. CodeSense keeps it in two places: the team's sprint registry, config/sprints.yaml (each sprint's state , goal , start , end and, once closed, delivered_points and carried_points ), and a sprint: field in each committed story's frontmatter. A planning agent, John here, running bmad-sprint-planning , reads the story graph and past velocity, proposes a commit list, and writes those two places once you accept it. You can edit them by hand too, or right-click a story in the left nav to Add to or Move to a sprint. The sprint-analysis.html example dashboard reads the registry and the stories live: velocity from closed sprints, and done versus committed points for the active one. A story's progress (todo → in-progress → review → done) comes straight from its status field. CodeSense doesn't run a sprint for you: agents pick up stories when you or a routine starts them.

entries.title: Massively parallel — shipping 5 stories at once
entries.text: Massively parallel — shipping 5 stories at once A sprint committed 5 stories. CodeSense creates 5 worktrees (one per story) via open_workspace . Each Amelia session binds to its own worktree + branch. Scout ( role_pending on scout ) catches a CI failure and inboxes the builder. Reviewer ( role_pending on reviewer ) picks up a merge-ready PR. The whole shape is N copies of the single-story loop , not a bespoke orchestration. All local 5 Amelias on your Mac Everything on-device. Fastest feedback loop, bounded by your CPU and the number of context windows you can open. Hybrid 2 local + 3 remote Keep the touchy ones local (where you want eyes on the diff) and offload the long-running builds to the private-account remote. All remote 5 remote tabs, drive from the laptop All five builders on the remote macbook. You drive from your laptop; merged work comes home through each story's PR. The three diagrams are specified at diagrams/sdlc/{all-local,hybrid,all-remote}.excalidraw.sketch.md .

entries.title: What this phase is for
entries.text: What this phase is for The best builder knows when to stop. If Amelia can't decide between two reasonable paths from the spec alone, she stops, escalates, and sleeps. bmad-loop-resolve wraps the escalation: it freezes the current spec state, posts a decision request to the resolver inbox, and resumes the builder when the answer lands. The resolver is often a human. On well-trodden paths, it's an agent (Winston or Mary) running the same skill with a wider context budget.

This is the phase where the retro of one epic drops a finding into the planning of the next: the kill-ladder's grace-period bug surfaced here and seeded the next-sprint DEMO-4 fix.

The agent publishes only after you say yes, and pushes only after that. Remote (private-account) A remote workspace publishes the same way: reverse_sync_worktree writes team content on this Mac. The push happens where the context repo's clone is, usually this Mac, so ask an agent here to push.

entries.text: How to do this via MCP // Preview, then publish the workspace's context edits. const target = { kind: 'local', codeRepoPath: '<worktree>', sessionId: '<session>' } codesense.invoke('preview_reverse_sync_worktree', { target }) codesense.invoke('reverse_sync_worktree', { target }) // Then run git yourself (commit, push) and report how it went. codesense.invoke('report_context_sync', { state: 'ok' })

entries.title: What this phase is for
entries.text: What this phase is for Shipping is a human-authorized moment, not a schedule. The agent previews its context edits with preview_reverse_sync_worktree , publishes them to team content with reverse_sync_worktree , then, when you ask, commits and pushes the context repo with git and reports with report_context_sync . Nothing publishes a workspace's edits on its own. Skip the publish and they stay on that machine.

entries.text: 14 LOOP Phase 14 · Loop The sweep that closes the factory loop. Run by a routine on a schedule, bmad-loop-sweep looks for work that fell through the cracks and carries it forward. Agent … Skill … Inbox … Trigger … Dashboard …

Remote (private-account) routine_arm_on moves the routine onto a remote machine, which then fires it on its own clock. Keep sweeps per-machine — a sweep that touches two context repos should emit its carry-over as inbox messages, not direct writes to the other machine.

entries.title: What this phase is for
entries.text: What this phase is for The loop phase is what makes CodeSense a factory, not a one-shot. bmad-loop-sweep runs on a schedule to catch everything that slipped: stories without owners, review threads gone cold, carried-over sprint points, retro findings nobody scheduled. A good sweep is short . If every run finds work, the earlier phases are under-planned; the retro of the next epic surfaces that pattern.

entries.title: From the itch to the ship
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Arc H · Pipelines + the full SDLC
entries.text: Arc H 14 phases pipelines + SDLC From the itch to the ship This arc shows one way to run the whole software development life cycle with agents in CodeSense: an idea becomes a spec, becomes an architecture, becomes stories, becomes pull requests, becomes a release. Each phase is one agent, one skill, one inbox role, one trigger, one dashboard. The agents do the work; CodeSense gives them the files, worktrees, inbox and tools. This arc walks every phase with the same seeded example so you can lift the shape into your own repo.

entries.title: How to use this arc
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Arc H · Pipelines + the full SDLC
entries.text: How to use this arc Read it top to bottom Start with phase 1 — idea and click through. Each page is a 5-minute read; the whole arc is a lunchtime. Jump to a phase you own A PM looking for sprint-planning mechanics should start at phase 6 ; a builder should start at phase 8 and loop back for context. Copy the agent + routine snippets Every phase shows a starting agent.yaml and, where the phase runs on a trigger, a routine.yml . Check them against the schemas below before you save them; an invalid agent.yaml refuses to load. Watch the dashboard breathe Keep factory playbook open in a split pane while you read; the content explains the model, the dashboard shows the state.

entries.title: What this arc covers
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Arc H · Pipelines + the full SDLC
entries.text: What this arc covers There are 14 phases in the CodeSense SDLC. The first seven are planning and design; phases 8–12 are build + verify; 13 and 14 are ship and loop. The agents are named: Mary analyses, Winston designs, Sally draws, John plans, Murat tests, Amelia builds, Resolver decides. Every page in this arc tells one phase's story with a worked example from the seeded DEMO epic. The skills named here ( bmad-create-epics-and-stories and the rest) come from BMAD, which you install in your own repo; CodeSense doesn't ship them. The phases are a pattern, not a gate: a story's status: is a plain field, nothing in CodeSense blocks a move between statuses, and each team sets its own statuses in Settings › Phases . You should read this arc end to end once, then come back when you need the detail for a specific phase. The live factory playbook dashboard shows the state of your own repo through the same lens.

entries.title: Runs and stories
entries.text: Arc H · Pipelines and SDLC Runs and stories Reference for the tools that read agent runs and run events, and for the story-authoring and source-repo tools: list_runs , read_run* , list_run_events , get_story_format , validate_story , read_epic_repos , set_epic_repos and list_source_repos .

entries.title: How a run joins its session
Agent runs
entries.text: Agent runs A run appears here once it has recorded an outcome. A run still going is not listed; list_sessions shows it. A dashboard's codesense.runs() , run() , runEvidence() and runWorkProduct() return the same data as the matching tools. list_runs Lists the latest recorded outcome of every agent run on this Mac, newest first by end time. Optional limit (default 50, max 500). Returns [{outcome:{story_id, run_id, status, summary?, ended_at, source, org?, team?, session_ids?, ...}, validated, has_structured_transcript, link}] . link is linked when the outcome names the session(s) that did the work ( session_ids , with the trusted org and team the run was launched under) and unlinked for a run recorded before outcomes carried them. Older runs are never rewritten. Take outcome.run_id to the other run tools, and outcome.session_ids to the session record (see How a run joins its session ). { "tool": "list_runs", "arguments": { "limit": 20 } } read_run Reads one run in full: {outcome, transcript, artifact, artifactTruncated} . transcript is the structured conversation or null (see How a session's conversation is kept ), artifact the tail of the captured terminal output (secrets redacted) or null. Optional maxArtifactBytes (default 65536, max 1048576) caps the output returned, from the end. outcome is the same row list_runs gives, with link . { "tool": "read_run", "arguments": { "runId": "<outcome.run_id from list_runs>" } } read_run_evidence Reads one run's audit record: {header, run, perNodeResults, authority} , covering what fired it, how it ended, its step-by-step spine and what each step reported. Returns null when there is no evidence. Optional storyId selects one story for a run that worked several. Use read_run for the transcript of a particular attempt. { "tool": "read_run_evidence", "arguments": { "runId": "<outcome.run_id from list_runs>" } } read_run_work_product Reads the git branch a run produced, as captured when it ended: {branch} , or null when it produced none, is still going or is unknown. The…

entries.title: How a session's conversation is kept
Source repos and epic repos
entries.text: Source repos and epic repos list_source_repos Lists the legal source_repo values and structured repository identities, including each repo's local clone ( attachment : attached , missing or unattached , plus localPath ). Use sourceRepoIdentities for explicit provider, host and remote key. Never invent a source_repo ; resolve it here. { "tool": "list_source_repos", "arguments": {} } read_epic_repos Reads the source repos an epic workspace is configured to assemble, from the epic doc's repos: frontmatter. Pass epicFilePath (the epic main-doc path, $CODESENSE_EPIC_DOC_PATH ). Returns an array of canonical owner/repo slugs, empty if none. Read-only. { "tool": "read_epic_repos", "arguments": { "epicFilePath": "/abs/path/to/epic.md" } } set_epic_repos Replaces the epic doc's repos: frontmatter. It is read-modify-write: pass the full desired repos list, not a delta (an empty list clears it); entries are normalised to owner/repo . Rejected if the target is not an epic doc. CodeSense then re-assembles the epic's integration worktrees in the background, and the call returns the re-read list immediately. { "tool": "set_epic_repos", "arguments": { "epicFilePath": "/abs/path/to/epic.md", "repos": [ "owner/repo" ] } }

entries.title: Authoring and validating stories
entries.text: Authoring and validating stories get_story_format Returns the decision-first contract for creating CodeSense content: whether frontmatter is needed at all (most content is a plain doc and needs none), the pipeline-story frontmatter schema, the validate_story finding codes, and cross-references to list_source_repos and validate_story . It takes no arguments; call it first. { "tool": "get_story_format", "arguments": {} } validate_story Validates a candidate file before it is written. Pass path (preferred, since it anchors depends_on and supporting_docs checks) and/or inline content . It detects the intent (plain doc, pipeline story or epic main doc) and does not nag a plain doc. For a story it returns blocking and advisory findings {code, field, severity, message, hint} , and never returns valid:true for a file it could not fully evaluate. { "tool": "validate_story", "arguments": { "path": "/abs/path/to/content/stories/DEMO-1.md" } }

entries.title: Approvals and assertions
entries.text: Approvals and assertions The endorsement gate: an agent assertion counts for nothing until the owning human ratifies it. wv_classify_action Returns the endorsement tier (T1, T2 or T3, with reasons) a proposed action would enter, without writing any row. Call it before wv_write_approval to branch on the tier. Inputs are claim , preferredTier and the risk signals irreversible , blastRadius and confidence . { "tool": "wv_classify_action", "arguments": { "claim": "Delete the stale branch", "preferredTier": "T2", "irreversible": true, "blastRadius": "low", "confidence": "high" } } wv_write_approval Opens an endorsement for a Tier-2 or Tier-3 action. tier is your preferred tier; the picker may force T3 when two of the three risk signals hold, and the chosen tier is what is stored and returned. Pass sessionId whenever the chosen tier could be T3. Returns {id, tier, disposition} . { "tool": "wv_write_approval", "arguments": { "tier": "T2", "claim": "Delete the stale branch", "irreversible": false, "blastRadius": "low", "confidence": "high", "sessionId": "<your $CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID>" } } wv_settle_approval Resolves a pending approval to ratified or revoked by id. It is the reply path for both T2 (window expiry) and T3 (owner approval). Idempotent: settling an already-settled or unknown id is a no-op. Returns {settled} . { "tool": "wv_settle_approval", "arguments": { "id": 3, "disposition": "ratified" } } wv_post_assertion Posts an agent assertion through the endorsement gate as a pending row that counts as nothing until the owning human ratifies it in the app. Inputs: sessionId , claim , channel , and an optional runId that must belong to the caller. The text in claim is scrubbed and size-bounded, and run provenance comes from the trusted session, not from arguments. Returns {id} . { "tool": "wv_post_assertion", "arguments": { "sessionId": "<your $CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID>", "claim": "Release notes are ready for review", "channel": "releases" } }

entries.title: Audit and posture
entries.text: Audit and posture wv_audit_query Reads the append-only write-audit trail, newest first, as [{id, tableName, operation, rowId, writtenAt}] . All filters are optional and ANDed: tableName , operation ( append or mutate ), sinceId / beforeId cursors, afterAt (epoch seconds). limit is clamped to 1–500 (default 100). Read-only, visible to all profiles. { "tool": "wv_audit_query", "arguments": { "tableName": "wv_queue", "limit": 50 } } wv_audit_prune Deletes audit rows with writtenAt before cutoffSecs (epoch seconds) and returns {pruned:<count>} . It is the only maintenance mutation on the trail, and it writes no audit row of its own. { "tool": "wv_audit_prune", "arguments": { "cutoffSecs": 1790000000 } } wv_read_posture Returns the scope's posture, {posture:"normal"|"away", windows:[{subclass, startMin, endMin}]} . A fresh store reads normal with no windows; a corrupt stored value falls back to normal . { "tool": "wv_read_posture", "arguments": {} } wv_set_posture Persists the posture, normal or away , with optional windows . When the value changes it triggers the matching Tier-2 pause or resume; setting the current value skips only the Tier-2 pause or resume; windows is always replaced, and an omitted windows becomes an empty list, so repeating {posture:"away"} clears any stored windows. Posture widens or narrows initiation and never grants authority. Returns {posture, changed, directive, windowsAffected} . { "tool": "wv_set_posture", "arguments": { "posture": "away" } }

entries.title: Dispatch and verification
entries.text: Dispatch and verification A dispatch is a four-field brief written before the worker starts, so the finish line is checkable rather than self-declared. wv_write_dispatch Writes a dispatch brief under a story_id key: task and acceptance (the Done-When) are required, context and constraints are optional, and scope is optional but only root is supported (the default). Any agent with this server can call it, a worker included. A dispatch with no checkable acceptance is refused. A brief is structural data, not instructions. Returns {id} . { "tool": "wv_write_dispatch", "arguments": { "story_id": "DEMO-13", "task": "Write the Weft coordination reference page", "acceptance": "The page names all 34 wv_* tools and its examples validate" } } wv_dispatch_state Reads the dispatch records for a story, newest first: {records:[{id, storyId, task, context, constraints, acceptance, state, scope, sessionId, createdAt, doneAt}]} . state is open or done . Read-only; it lets a reader check what finished means without asking the worker. { "tool": "wv_dispatch_state", "arguments": { "story_id": "DEMO-13" } } wv_handoff_state Reads the drafted handoff packets for a story, newest first: {records:[{id, storyId, sessionId, toRole, finding, refs, isDraft, createdAt}]} . Each packet is data, not authority ( isDraft is always true). Read-only. { "tool": "wv_handoff_state", "arguments": { "story_id": "DEMO-13" } } wv_verify_done Re-checks a worker's three-leg done record before its queue row is folded: source-aware, in-scope work finished, packet delivered idempotently. Stamps controllerVerified only when every leg passes. Returns {verified, reason, failedLegs} ; a dispatch with no done record returns verified:false with all three legs failed, because idle is not done. { "tool": "wv_verify_done", "arguments": { "dispatchId": "dispatch-1" } } wv_read_recent Observes a worker's recent terminal output as plain text. Pass the opaque handle the dispatch returned, not a session id. Returns {text, seq, altScreen} : altScreen is true while a…

entries.title: Weft coordination tools
entries.text: Arc H · Pipelines and SDLC Weft coordination tools Reference for the Weft coordination tools ( wv_* ): the Weft queue, dispatch briefs, approvals, Tier-2 windows, the decision and attention ledger, and the audit and posture controls.

entries.title: How to read this page
entries.text: How to read this page Each entry says what the tool does, how it differs from its neighbours, and shows one call with the wire names the server expects. Results are described only where the served description names them. These tools are mechanisms: which of them to use, and in what order, is the agent's decision. Where a tool takes sessionId , the verified MCP connection supplies identity; a supplied sessionId must name the caller itself, and an unbound caller is refused.

entries.title: Decisions, attention and watches
entries.text: Decisions, attention and watches The Weft ledger: standing decisions, items waiting on a human, per-source read watermarks and per-scope watches. wv_write_decision Writes a bounded standing decision. Required: date , decision , constrains (the one artifact it binds) and endsWhen (the retirement condition; a blank one is refused). The stored owner is the verified caller. Returns {id} . { "tool": "wv_write_decision", "arguments": { "date": "2026-10-23", "decision": "Docs pages describe mechanisms only", "constrains": "codesense-docs reference pages", "endsWhen": "The docs policy is replaced" } } wv_retire_decision Marks a standing decision superseded by id so the triage intent-check stops matching it. Idempotent: an already-superseded or unknown id is a no-op. Returns {retired} . { "tool": "wv_retire_decision", "arguments": { "id": 12 } } wv_list_overdue_harvests Lists active decisions still pending (no drafted artifact) whose date is more than 24 hours before nowUnix (epoch seconds). An agent reads them to draft the missing artifact. Read-only. Returns [{id, date, decision, constrains, endsWhen, owner, source}] . { "tool": "wv_list_overdue_harvests", "arguments": { "nowUnix": 1792800000 } } wv_upsert_attention Writes an item that needs a human response into the attention ledger the Board reads. Omit id to create (a non-blank summary is required; state defaults to needs-you ); pass id to update state ( needs-you , waiting or done-unacked ). Returns {id} . { "tool": "wv_upsert_attention", "arguments": { "summary": "Approve the release notes", "state": "needs-you", "source": "github", "reference": "owner/repo#123" } } wv_upsert_watermark Advances the read watermark for a (source, scope) key; source is slack , jira , github , local or agent . A second call on the same key advances lastHandled rather than inserting a duplicate. Returns {ok:true} . { "tool": "wv_upsert_watermark", "arguments": { "source": "github", "scope": "sprint-1", "lastHandled": "comment-4812" } } wv_scope_state Reads a scope's ledger row plus its…

entries.title: Peer reads
entries.text: Peer reads Bounded read access to a peer worker. Both tools are authorised only when your dispatch lists the peer under peers: . wv_coord_read Reads a peer's wv_coord contract body. Pass sessionId and contract . Returns {body} , {error:"not-authorized"} when your dispatch does not list the owner, or {error:"not-found"} . Coord is state, never a message or an approval. { "tool": "wv_coord_read", "arguments": { "sessionId": "<your $CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID>", "contract": "api-shape" } } wv_peer_read_file Reads one file from a peer's worktree. Pass sessionId , peerName and relPath (relative to the peer's root). A path containing .. returns {error:"path-traversal"} ; files over 256 KB return {error:"too-large", sizeBytes} . Success returns {contentUtf8} ; other results are binary , not-found and peer-not-found errors. { "tool": "wv_peer_read_file", "arguments": { "sessionId": "<your $CODESENSE_TAB_SESSION_ID>", "peerName": "worker-a", "relPath": "docs/guide.md" } }

entries.title: Queue
entries.text: Queue The Weft queue holds work items as rows that move through pending , claimed and dispatched . Resolved rows are pruned and never appear in a listing. wv_enqueue Adds a pending row to the Weft queue for an agent to claim; triage may write it. Pass source , and optionally scope , refs , note and dedupeKey . With a dedupeKey , a second enqueue while a live row with that key exists is a no-op that returns the existing id, so a trigger can call it on every pulse. Returns {id} ; row ids are not stable across prunes. { "tool": "wv_enqueue", "arguments": { "source": "triage", "scope": "sprint-1", "note": "Review request for DEMO-13", "dedupeKey": "review:DEMO-13" } } wv_queue_list Lists the non-resolved queue rows ( pending , claimed , dispatched ), optionally filtered by scope . Read-only. Returns [{id, source, state, claimedBy, scope, created, updated, refs, note}] . Use it to look at the queue; use wv_claim_queue to take a row. { "tool": "wv_queue_list", "arguments": { "scope": "sprint-1" } } wv_claim_queue Claims one pending queue row and evaluates the keep/delegate tripwire in one step. Both verdicts stamp the verified owner as claimedBy . Optional evidence ( scope , touchedPaths , addedLines , persistent , requiresDiffRead ) feeds the tripwire; with no evidence it keeps the item. The store follows the caller's captured team, and callers without one, or unbound callers, are refused. delegateRunId is correlation only and never grants ownership. Returns {claimed:true, id, verdict, firedRow, claimedBy, delegateRunId} or {claimed:false} ; losing a concurrent claim reports claimLost . { "tool": "wv_claim_queue", "arguments": { "scope": "sprint-1", "touchedPaths": [ { "path": "docs/guide.md" } ], "addedLines": 12 } } wv_mark_dispatched Marks a claimed row dispatched once a worker is running; only the verified owner of the row can do this, and unbound callers are refused. The order is claim, write the brief with wv_write_dispatch , spawn the worker, then this call with queueId , storyId (the brief key) and…

entries.title: Tier-2 windows
entries.text: Tier-2 windows A Tier-2 approval carries a revocation window. The clock freezes while the owner is away. wv_open_t2_window Arms the lazy-consent window on a pending T2 approval. It records surfacedSession (the session the item was shown to the owner in; the window may auto-close only when later checked in this same session), the open time on the server clock, and durationS , the present-time budget. It is rejected if the id is not a pending T2, surfacedSession is blank, or durationS is not positive. Returns {opened:true} . { "tool": "wv_open_t2_window", "arguments": { "id": 3, "surfacedSession": "<surfacing session id>", "durationS": 3600 } } wv_check_t2_window Evaluates a window at the server clock without changing it. A spent budget reports lapsed only when checkSession matches the surfacing session; otherwise expiredWrongSession . Returns {state, elapsedS, remainingS} where state is notOpen , open , paused , expiredWrongSession or lapsed . { "tool": "wv_check_t2_window", "arguments": { "id": 3, "checkSession": "<surfacing session id>" } } wv_close_t2_window Auto-ratifies a T2 approval whose window has lapsed, only when checkSession matches the surfacing session. A paused, open, wrong-session, revoked or already-settled window is a no-op, and an owner's explicit reply is never overwritten. Returns {ratified} . { "tool": "wv_close_t2_window", "arguments": { "id": 3, "checkSession": "<surfacing session id>" } } wv_pause_t2_windows Freezes the clock of every live T2 window at the server time. Idempotent: an already-paused window is skipped. Returns {paused: <count>} . wv_set_posture calls this on the move to away. { "tool": "wv_pause_t2_windows", "arguments": {} } wv_resume_t2_windows The counterpart of the pause: banks each paused span into the window's accumulated pause, then restarts the clocks. Idempotent. Returns {resumed: <count>} . { "tool": "wv_resume_t2_windows", "arguments": {} }

entries.title: The allowlist contract
entries.text: The allowlist contract invoke accepts only the page-bridge verbs. Anything else is refused before it reaches the app — there is no route to a raw command. MCP tool names such as list_orgs_teams are for agents, not pages; a page that calls one gets … is not allowlisted . Each verb needs a capability grant (for example inbox:write ); a call without it is refused with denied: grant . By default an allowlisted verb with its grant runs without a confirm sheet. The team-safe preset and per-dashboard settings add confirm sheets for destructive or send-as-you verbs, and loadMedia always asks. The classes below decide which calls are logged and which runaway limit applies. Writes are confined by the app itself — a page can only edit content CodeSense manages, so a write into the read-only docs org is refused. files.delete and files.move are allowed by default: a page that holds the grant can delete or move team content files without a confirm sheet. Dashboards are your own files and run with the app's page APIs, so open only dashboards you trust (see How CodeSense trusts agents ). Both verbs are confirmable, so a per-dashboard setting can make each call wait for the person. If they decline, nothing is deleted or moved, and the page's promise resolves with {status: "cancelled"} rather than rejecting. After an approval it resolves with {status: "confirmed", result: ...} . To set it, edit app-state.json in the app's data directory ( ~/Library/Application Support/ai.codesense/app-state.json for the macOS app) and add the verbs under your profile's dashboardPolicy.perDashboard , keyed by the dashboard's exact identity. The profile section is localProfileWorkspacesV1 keyed by your local principal, the same numeric user id the app shows for your account. Change only these fields and keep everything else in the file, including other profiles. The app watches the file, and the policy is read on every dispatch, so the next files.delete or files.move call uses the new setting; see Configuration is live too . The key is not the…

entries.title: The core call
entries.text: The core call invoke(verb, args) takes a verb name (a string) and an args object. The promise resolves with whatever the verb returns. A failure rejects with a plain Error whose message starts with a stable prefix you can branch on: try { const here = await codesense.invoke("context", {}); render(here); // { org, team, layer, contentRoot }, or null outside every content root } catch (err) { // err.message starts with one of: // '… is not allowlisted' — the verb isn't a bridge verb // 'denied: write budget' — too many writes in a short window (also send, spawn, prefs) // 'busy' — too many agent launches already running // 'unavailable: …' — the backend for this verb is down // or it is the app's own refusal, word for word. if (err.message.endsWith("is not allowlisted")) showFallback(); else throw err; } The invoke tab of the explorer lists every verb with its arguments.

entries.title: One call. A promise. A clear error.
entries.text: Arc I · Bridge One call. A promise. A clear error. Every action a dashboard performs — read the inbox, open a workspace, send a message, start a routine — goes through one function: window.codesense.invoke(verb, args) . It returns a Promise . It resolves with the result shape documented in the explorer, or rejects with an error whose message you can match on. Most named methods you'll meet ( codesense.openFile , codesense.inbox , codesense.worktrees ) are thin wrappers over invoke . Calling CodeSense — invoke round-trip your doc codesense.invoke (verb, args) bridge allowlist allowlist · audit host tauri command invoke dispatch result · err resolve · reject doc · bridge · host · bridge · doc — one correlated round-trip

entries.title: Write for older apps too
entries.text: Write for older apps too A team's panes and dashboards reach every teammate, including people whose app has not updated yet. A page that uses a member their app lacks stops with a TypeError before it finishes loading. Before you use a member the oldest supported app lacks, check that it exists. Calling it, reading through it, reading it into a variable and destructuring it are all uses. Any of these checks works: codesense.onTeardown?.(stop); if (typeof codesense.onFlush === "function") codesense.onFlush(save); async function load() { if (!codesense.subscribe) return showNotice("Update CodeSense to see this list."); render(await codesense.subscribe("sessions", { onChange: render })); } const kit = codesense.kit; const list = typeof kit.virtualList === "function" ? kit.virtualList({ container, rows, render }) : null; list?.setRows(rows); The check must sit at the use: in the same condition, an earlier return in the same block, or a const that holds the test. A check made elsewhere does not count. The release check follows codesense through variables and function parameters; a parameter named cs , codesense or kit is treated as the API or its kit even when the caller is not visible. When a feature is missing, say so on the page (for example "This view needs a newer CodeSense") rather than leaving it empty. With a check, an older app shows the page without that feature, and a current app works as before. The oldest supported app is CodeSense 0.0.25. Every supported app has these members, so they need no check: act , agent , agents , context , firstPaint , getNavSelection , humanStatus , inbox , invoke , kit , machines , modelRates , onAgentsChanged , onInboxChanged , onMachinesChanged , onNavSelectionChange , onRoutineResult , onRoutinesChanged , onSessions , onTheme , onVisibility , onWorktreesChanged , openFile , prefs , queryContext , readWorkspace , roles , routine , routineCancel , routineRefresh , routineResult , routineRun , routineRuns , routineStatus , routines , run , runEvidence , runWorkProduct , runs ,…

entries.title: Three canonical patterns
entries.text: Three canonical patterns Read something and render it The simplest shape. Read once, render, done. Keep page-load calls to read verbs; anything that writes or launches belongs behind a button. codesense.worktrees().then((wts) => { for (const wt of wts) renderRow(wt); }); Act on a click A write or a launch runs as soon as you call it, so put it behind a button the person clicks: <button id="go">Open DEMO-12</button> <script> document.getElementById("go").addEventListener("click", () => codesense.invoke("openWorkspace", { storyId: "DEMO-12" }), ); </script> Subscribe and re-read Live dashboards wrap the read in a function and let a nudge event trigger it. See reacting to state for the full pattern — the short version: function reload() { codesense.inbox().then(render); } reload(); codesense.onInboxChanged(reload);

entries.title: Spend caps require a person to loosen
entries.text: Spend caps require a person to loosen Agent and routine reads include budgetUsd , budgetPending and spend . An edit through MCP or an embedded page can tighten a cap immediately; raising or removing it only saves a pending request. The native app's Spend cap controls are the acceptance surface. Pages cannot invoke the native set or accept commands. This enforcement covers CodeSense surfaces. Agents run as you; give an agent you don't fully trust sandboxed permissions. See the Architecture boundary and How CodeSense trusts agents . setModelRate changes that lower counted spend, including pricing an unpriced model, also stay pending until native acceptance. Raising rates applies immediately. See Spend caps .

entries.title: Tool reference
entries.text: Tool reference Reference for MCP tools that act on the app's panes: commands, rendered documents, canvases and workspace card order. The page verb codesense.commands.list() returns the same rows as command_list , and codesense.commands.run(id, args) does what command_run does. Commands command_list Lists the commands the slot dashboards (right-pane, dock and file-nav) declare that you may run: [{id, label, scope, binding, dashboard, active, humanOnly}] . id is what command_run takes. scope is where the person's chord fires and does not limit command_run . active is false while the dashboard has narrowed its commands with codesense.commands.register ; an inactive command cannot run. A dashboard whose policy grant lacks commands:run is left out. { "tool": "command_list", "arguments": {} } command_run Runs a slot dashboard's command by id from command_list , with optional args for the page. The app reveals the dashboard's slot if it is closed and delivers the command once, after the page is ready, as the person's chord does. Returns {requested:true} once dispatched; the page acts on its own. Refused with denied: grant when the dashboard's policy grant lacks commands:run , denied: ... is for humans only for a humanOnly command, unavailable: for an inactive one, and unknown command for an id command_list does not list. { "tool": "command_run", "arguments": { "id": "<id from command_list>", "args": {} } } Rendered documents and canvases read_rendered_document Reads an already-open HTML document or team/private pane's rendered DOM, without writing an archive or refreshing data. Select the document tab or show the pane in the main window first, and use the absolute path from pane_list ; closed, hidden and fallback panes return actionable errors. format is text (default, readable text) or html (frozen serialized HTML with injected scripts removed). Returns sourcePath , format , content , capturedAt and truncated (512 KiB cap). It is point-in-time DOM content, not a screenshot, and it never opens documents, runs…

entries.title: Try this now
entries.text: Try this now Click the button to call context from this page: the org, team and folder this page lives in. Read-only.

entries.title: How to do this via MCP
entries.text: How to do this via MCP Agent-side equivalent Pages and agents reach the same app through different doors. A page calls bridge verbs; an agent calls MCP tools. Many read verbs have an MCP twin: # Page await codesense.invoke("worktrees", {}); # Agent (MCP tool) list_worktrees {} Browse the pairing in ui-mcp-crossref .

entries.title: How to do this via MCP
One call. A promise. A clear error.
Spend caps require a person to loosen
Declare and register
entries.text: Declare and register <meta name="codesense:commands" content='[{"id":"toggle-filter","label":"Toggle running sessions","scope":"slot-focused","defaultChord":"CmdOrCtrl+Alt+L","humanOnly":false}]'> <script> const cs = window.codesense; cs.onCommand(command => { if (command.id === 'toggle-filter') toggleFilter(); }); cs.ready(); cs.commands.register(['toggle-filter']).catch(showError); </script> Install handlers before calling ready() or subscribe() . Registration activates only declared ids. Delivery is queued until explicit readiness or an admitted subscription marks the frame live. Subscription admission can release commands before its initial snapshot resolves; the shim's automatic transport handshake does not count. Each dispatch has a dispatchId and is delivered at most once.

entries.title: Commands, chords and menus
entries.text: Arc I · Pane authoring Commands, chords and menus Declare commands once, register handlers in the page, and let the host deliver chords, palette actions and native menus.

entries.title: Peek at an agent's terminal
entries.text: Peek at an agent's terminal Ask the host for agent-quick-send to open a themed quick view beside an agent row. The host owns the frame, terminal and positioning above the workspace bar. Open tab opens the agent's CLI tab. A terminal already visible in the CLI stays there; the quick view offers Show in CLI instead. const button = document.querySelector('#peek'); button.addEventListener('click', () => { const { x, y, width, height } = button.getBoundingClientRect(); window.codesense.showPopover({ kind: 'agent-quick-send', anchorId: button.id, anchorRect: { x, y, width, height }, row: { kind: 'agent', sessionId: session.sessionId } }); }); Typing goes straight to the agent's terminal. Escape inside it goes to the CLI; Escape on the header controls closes the quick view. ⌘W and Close return focus to the invoking button. An outside click closes it where the person clicked. The resize corner remembers the size and also accepts arrow keys.

entries.title: Native row menus
entries.text: Native row menus const row = document.createElement('li'); row.dataset.codesenseRow = JSON.stringify({kind: 'agent', sessionId: session.id}); row.textContent = session.displayName; // A right click asks the host for the native agent menu. Keep normal text selection. data-codesense-row identifies a row to the native menu builder. Story/file paths are relative to the bound team's content root. Use the SDK's ContextMenuRow union for row shapes. Unknown or unresolved rows fall back to the dashboard menu. Text fields and selected text get native text menus first. For a custom button menu call showMenu({anchorRect, anchorId, row, items}) ; anchorRect is the button's bounding rect and anchorId lets focus return to it. Page-local item ids return to your handler. The host owns builtin:reload-pane , builtin:open-as-tab , builtin:edit-source , builtin:stop , builtin:close-tab and builtin:set-role ; use only actions applicable to that row or dashboard. Built-ins retain their native validation and confirmation. See the golden live sessions example for a native row menu without a copied implementation.

entries.title: Scope and rebinding
entries.text: Scope and rebinding global commands are available globally, slot-visible requires a visible slot, and slot-focused requires focus in its slot for the keyboard shortcut. defaultChord is the initial binding, not a guarantee: reserved or conflicting shortcuts may be unbound. The person can rebind or clear it in Settings → Shortcuts. Use the generated declaration contract for accepted scopes and fields. humanOnly:true permits the person's palette/chord and page command invocation but refuses agent command_run . For an agent-verifiable command, leave it false. Agents discover the full dashboard/command id with command_list and pass that exact id to command_run . The host reveals a hidden target before delivering. On a dock team rebind the SDK holds calls, adopts the new grant and resyncs topics; handle onSlotContext to drop your own old-team state.

entries.text: Arc I · Pane authoring Add a custom pane with a live list and a command Five steps from a single HTML file to a visible, verifiable pane. Start with the golden live sessions example; no source checkout or bundler is needed.

entries.crumb: CodeSense — Add a custom pane with a live list and a command
entries.text: 5. Share the file A team pane is a file in the context repository. Review the diff, then share through whatever git sync workflow you and the user choose. CodeSense provides git state and sync tools; the agent decides when to commit and push. Private panes remain in the person's space unless deliberately copied to a team. Keep the validation and visible before/after evidence with your handoff.

entries.title: Keep live rows stable
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Add a custom pane with a live list and a command
entries.text:
Keep live rows stable Load /kit/v1/virtual-list.js after the kit. Each row needs a stable id . Split its layout payload from live fields: layoutKey(row) returns a string or number describing the markup, while update(element, row, index) patches every reused row on each paint. Initialize the same fields in render . Heartbeats, counts and status changes then keep hover, focus and selection on the same node.
This layout always has the same two spans, so its stable id is sufficient. If your markup changes, return JSON.stringify([row.id, row.kind, row.hasActions]) instead. The kit compares the returned value as a string and rebuilds only that row when it changes. update receives the current index after an insert or remove; indexes never determine row versions. Tree ARIA attributes and roving tab stops are refreshed each paint. Omit layoutKey to rebuild on any row payload change (the default). The same options work with topic: "sessions" instead of local rows ; the kit requests the visible hub window. For an unwindowed list, kit.keyed(container, items, {key, render, version, update}) patches same-key, same-version nodes with update(element, item) ; changed versions call render . Keep…

entries.title: 4. Verify visible behavior
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Add a custom pane with a live list and a command
entries.text: 4. Verify visible behavior read_rendered_document {path:"<absolute pane_list path>", format:"text"} command_list {} command_run {id:"<the returned dashboard/command id for toggle-filter>"} read_rendered_document {path:"<the same absolute pane path>", format:"text"} The first capture should show “All sessions”; after running the command it should show “Running only” and the changed row count/list. This feedback works even when the team has no sessions. Commands are delivered after readiness. Allow capture after the command has rendered; if necessary take another point-in-time read. A refusal explains whether to open/show the pane or fix its fallback. Wait beyond the 30-second startup deadline and capture again to check it stays live. Also try the visible filter button, its configured chord and an agent row's native menu. Those human interactions need a real-app walk; report them as unproven until performed. See proof boundaries .

entries.title: Save and preview your fork
entries.text: Save and preview your fork Read the selected example as text. Give its <title> a recognizable name, such as Backend triage . Before overwriting an existing custom pane, call pane_list for the intended org/team, find that fork’s returned path , and use ordinary local filesystem access to read it and copy a backup outside every panes/ directory . A backup HTML left in panes/ becomes another discoverable pane. There is no pane-read MCP tool; do not assume read_content_file accepts pane paths. Use a distinct id for the first preview, such as backend-triage-preview . For a right-pane preview of the agent list, change its codesense:slots from dock to right-pane dock . Keep Notes’ right-pane declaration. Inbox uses its human-inbox surface. Keep the original capabilities, commands, event handlers, visibility handling and cleanup. Check declarations , SDK methods , exact typings , grants and slot ceilings rather than copying a permission table. Declaring a capability requests it; policy and the slot still bound the effective grant. Notes reads your private records; a team-safe pane may be denied them. Never work around a denial by broadening policy. Call validate_live_data_doc with { content: html } for the edited HTML (or { path: localFilePath } to validate a local file), resolve its diagnostics, then pane_write with the whole document. pane_write overwrites a file; it does not merge edits. Use scope: "personal" only when the user requests a private fork; the tool calls this scope “personal”, while discovery labels it “private”. Call pane_open with the same id and scope. Confirm placed: true ; otherwise switch to the named team or a child team (or the private fork’s org), then call it again. The fork is a separate panel. Use View → Panels and its title to show it again. // Agent-side MCP calls. html is the complete copied and edited document. mcp.call("validate_live_data_doc", { content: html }) mcp.call("pane_write", { org: "acme/api", scope: "personal", id: "backend-triage-preview", html }) mcp.call("pane_open", {…

entries.text: Arc I · Recipe Customize the built-in panes Fork the Inbox pane, Notes or agent list pane from the exact HTML shipped with this app. To customize Inbox, start with its complete source and keep the live plumbing.

entries.title: Customize the Inbox pane: one team’s needs-you queue
entries.text: Customize the Inbox pane: one team’s needs-you queue In the Inbox copy, use your real org and team in place of acme/api and backend . This queue works while that team is active and intentionally shows an error asking you to switch teams elsewhere. Promoting it to a private canonical Inbox affects every team you open in that org; promoting it to a team Inbox also affects child teams. Other teams’ Inbox entry points will show that error, not their mail. Keep it as a distinct-id side panel if that broader effect is unwanted. It explicitly binds every read and write to that pair, including history paging, and uses the real message kind . Unread is a separate property. Here “needs-you” filters the conversation list : an extra query supplies eligibility, unread counts and previews from the latest 500 matching needs-you messages. Opening one shows the complete conversation , including updates and your replies. The pane badge keeps the shipped full-Inbox unread count; the list counts only matching needs-you messages. Keep the shipped unfiltered message windows, conversation summaries, history cursors and paging unchanged. The small derived list view below does not filter thread messages or rewrite summary counts. @@ - const contextReady = cs.context().then((ctx) => { + let triageMessages = []; + const triageTeam = { org: "acme/api", team: "backend" }; + const contextReady = cs.context().then((host) => { + const current = host.activeTeam || { org: host.org, team: host.team }; + if (current.org !== triageTeam.org || current.team !== triageTeam.team) + throw new Error("Switch to the triage team before opening this Inbox"); + const ctx = { ...host, ...triageTeam }; @@ - crossTeam = ctx.inboxScope === "all-teams"; + crossTeam = false; @@ - const writeTeam = (team) => (crossTeam ? team : {}); + const writeTeam = () => triageTeam; @@ - const [inbox, sent, roleView, status] = await Promise.all([ + const [inbox, sent, roleView, status, queue] = await Promise.all([ @@ - crossTeam ? cs.inboxRollup?.() : cs.inbox({ scope:…

entries.title: Notes: count the pinned section
entries.text: Notes: count the pinned section Notes already separates pinned and recent notes. partitionNotes() reads fields.pinned , sorts pinned notes by title, and keeps recent notes separate. Make a small useful variation: include the current pinned count in its section heading. In renderList() , replace the pinned entry in the section loop: @@ - ["Pinned", pinned], + [`Pinned (${pinned.length})`, pinned], This counts the current search results. With no search, it counts all pinned notes. Empty groups remain hidden. Keep the real Pin/Unpin menu: it writes the note’s existing metadata through the records API. Pin or unpin a note and confirm the section and count update live. Keep records subscriptions and editor lifecycle unchanged; there is no separate pin store or pin API.

entries.title: Select the fork and restore the original
entries.text: Select the fork and restore the original Replace the Inbox entry point After the distinct-id preview works, write the same edited HTML with the canonical id: "inbox" , in the requested private or team scope. Use the Inbox entry in View → Panels (or the Inbox shortcut) to reveal it. With no explicit profile choice, Inbox resolves the nearest team-chain inbox , then your private inbox , then the bundled built-in. A team fork therefore takes precedence over a private fork: a private inbox will not replace an existing team inbox . Sharing a team-scoped id: "inbox" replaces that team’s Inbox for everyone using its content, including inheriting child teams. Coordinate that change with the team before sharing it. An existing explicit profile selection takes precedence over this automatic lookup; writing a canonical file does not change that selection. See the saved-choice check below if your fork does not appear. To revert, delete or rename your fork’s panes/inbox.html at the path returned by pane_write , or copy the outside- panes/ backup back to that exact path if there was already a custom Inbox. Reveal Inbox again after discovery updates. Removing a private fork returns to the bundled Inbox only if no team fork or explicit profile choice still wins. Identify the original by dashboardRef.scope: "built-in" and its app-owned path, {codesense_home}/users/{principal}/builtin-panes/panes/inbox.html . Its outer pane_list entry can say scope: "private" ; that label alone does not make it your custom fork. Do not edit or delete that original or the docs example. There is no “classic Inbox” toggle. If a saved Inbox choice still wins Inspect the local profile JSON with ordinary filesystem access at {codesense_home}/users/{principal}/scratch/orgs/{owner}/{repo}/config/profile.json . Look at rightPaneSurfaces.inbox and slots["right-pane"] , and match any saved reference against the full dashboardRef in pane_list , including its scope and team. Use that listing’s exact path to identify the selected custom file. A private…

entries.title: Start with the shipped source
entries.text: Start with the shipped source These are read-only examples, generated from the current implementations. Each begins with a “Fork me” provenance comment; every remaining byte matches its source. Copy the whole file, including its scripts and declarations, into your own pane. Editing an example in the docs team does not customize the app. Inbox HTML — src/features/shell/right-pane/__fixtures__/inbox-pane.html . This is the built-in HTML Inbox the app ships. Notes HTML — src/features/shell/right-pane/__fixtures__/notes-pane.html . An HTML alternative; the app can also use classic Notes. Follow the function names in these copies and apply the edits below. The source paths explain provenance, not a dependency on a developer workspace.

entries.title: Keep the fork current
entries.text: Keep the fork current App updates refresh these generated examples, not your customized copy. Keep the original snapshot and your small diff; compare a new example against it before carrying your edit forward. Revalidate and repeat the live checks after updating. Saving your pane prepares a replacement behind its frozen working view and swaps only when ready. A broken save keeps the previous version interactive under a fallback strip; hidden panes catch up on reveal. See pane saves and the optional state snapshot . Preserve subscriptions, teardown, commands and stable row ids rather than building another state store. Continue with a custom live list , pane shapes , commands and menus , lifecycle and liveness , records and testing and conformance . See also generated live topics and exact MCP tool arguments .

The pieces
entries.text: The pieces Call What you get CS.boot({render, queries, key}) One entry for both hosts. render(ctx) runs at once, from cached answers, and again whenever a query changes; keep it idempotent. ctx.host is "app" or "hosted" . Returns {host, call, subscribe, state, refresh, stop} . CS.cachedQuery(name, args, {maxAgeMs, key}) peek() gives {value, ageMs, state} with state one of cached (from storage, younger than maxAgeMs ), stale (older; one read is revalidating it), fresh (just read) or none (nothing yet). A failed read keeps the value and sets error . Storage is keyed by host, dashboard key and args; a frame with no storage uses memory. maxAgeMs is required. CS.visibleTotals(container, {rowSelector, idAttr, root}) Gathers the ids of visible rows, batches and debounces them into storyTotals , and caches each id with its computedAtMs . A pending id, or one that failed in a way that clears by itself, is asked again with backoff (2, 4, 8, then every 16 s) while it is visible. A row that already shows values and is only refreshing is asked at most every 60 s, backing off to 240 s, while it is visible. An id that was never in view is never asked. Hiding or showing the page, or rows coming back into view, asks nothing for an id that was already asked: only an id never asked (or one a data-change event named while off screen) is asked when it scrolls in, and a pending row that scrolls back in is picked up by the follow-up timer. An ask refused for some ids is halved down to the single ids refused; only a refusal of the whole verb ( query_not_declared , not_declared , undeclared , access_ended , a verb that is not allowlisted) is known from one ask. arg_not_allowed on many ids is probed with the first, middle and last id in one round: if all three are refused before the page has had any answer, the page is treated as unpinned (every id refused, one console warning) until refresh({refused: true}) , so check the storyIds pin in your manifest. That is a deliberate trade-off: a page whose first, middle and last visible ids are…

entries.title: What the checker flags
entries.text: What the checker flags Rule Shape Fix F1 (reported now; the publisher will refuse it) script[src] or currentScript in dashboard code CS.boot F4 a detail query ( storyChanges , whyLine ) inside a loop over rows CS.visibleTotals for the list, CS.section for detail F5 ?? 0 or || 0 on a nullable total CS.value F8 waitForTimeout or a real-time sleep in a browser test advance page.clock F10 a query without limit pass a limit K6+ a list page that reads totals without visibleTotals and budget ; CS.section inside a row loop; cachedQuery without maxAgeMs use the patterns above

entries.title: A complete example
entries.text:
A complete example A story list that opens warm, asks totals for the rows on screen and reads a story's commits only when its section opens. The same file runs in the app and on a shared page: load cs-live.js there (or nothing extra in the app, where the kit is injected).
Commits

entries.title: Handles and options
entries.text: Handles and options Call Handle and options CS.cachedQuery Returns {peek(), refresh(), onChange(cb), ready} . refresh() reads again and resolves the new peek() ; onChange(cb) calls cb(result) on each answer or failure and returns an unsubscribe; ready is the promise of the read in flight. Asking again for the same name, args and key returns the same handle; the same with another maxAgeMs gets its own (same stored answer, own label). On a shared page the frame is sandboxed (an opaque origin) and has no storage, so the answer is kept in memory for the page's life : warm within the page, not across loads. CS.section Options: key , load , render , when , scope , isEmpty(value) (default: an empty array or null), emptyText , stillMs (default 15000). Returns {refresh(), cancel(), stop(), loaded} . A section reads once: after Cancel or an error it shows that again however often it scrolls back in, and only Retry or Refresh (a small button once a read is a minute old), dataChanged({keys}) naming it, or its busy backoff reads again. A render that throws shows "Could not show this." CS.visibleTotals Options: rowSelector , idAttr (default data-id ), root , debounceMs , onChange(handle) (after each answer), onError(err) (a failed ask; it is asked again with backoff). Returns {get(id), ids(), known(), refresh({refused}), changed(ids), stop()} . stop() cancels its reads in flight. CS.keyedRegion Returns {paint(items, {key, render, version, update}, forScope), setScope(scope), text, defer, flush, stop()} . Without version a row's version is the JSON of its item, so a changed row repaints. setScope(next) names the scope that may paint now; a paint for another scope is dropped. kit.call The raw bridge verb, in the app only, and not budgeted : use it for actions. Reads go through kit.query , queryAll , storyTotals and the patterns above, which share the budget. Bytes are counted only when bytesPerMinute is set or ?csmeter=1 is on.

entries.title: Fast, light dashboards
entries.text: Arc I · Dashboard patterns Fast, light dashboards A dashboard that opens at once and never floods the Mac: a cached list, totals only for the rows on screen, and each section reading when it is opened. The patterns are in the kit already, with the same names in the app ( codesense.kit , also window.CS ) and on a shared page ( CS ). Use them instead of writing your own cache, queue or loading states.

entries.title: Tabbing away and back never reloads
entries.text: Tabbing away and back never reloads A dashboard's state stays in memory and shows at once when you come back. The kit makes no read on visibilitychange , focus , blur , pageshow or online : hiding the page only pauses timers (poll intervals, totals follow-ups), and showing it only starts them again. A section that has read shows it again however long the page was hidden or scrolled away. Write your own page the same way: never read from those events.

entries.title: Live data patches in place
entries.text: Live data patches in place A data-change event names what changed, and only that is read again. CS.dataChanged({ids, keys}) asks visibleTotals again for the visible rows named by ids (one ask, just those ids; the others are marked and asked when they scroll in) and re-reads only the sections named by keys , quietly, in place; paint the result with CS.keyedRegion so only the changed rows move. In the app, a hub codesense:delta carries the ids ( upserts[].id and removes ). The payloadless nudges ( agent-activity-changed , worktrees-changed and the like) and the hosted viewer and subscribe notices carry none, so they name nothing: nothing requeries a whole list or story on an event. Call refresh() yourself, deliberately, when you want everything again.

entries.title: Six rules
entries.text: Six rules One entry, one boot. CS.boot picks the host from the bridge that is present. Never test script[src] , currentScript or a file name: the share host strips every script src , and the page would stay blank. Paint the last answer first. Read the list with CS.cachedQuery . It paints from storage at once, then reads once. Ask totals for visible rows only. CS.visibleTotals watches the rows and asks one storyTotals call for the ids on screen. Read detail when it is opened. CS.section loads a <details> or a region when it opens or scrolls into view, with its own states. One budget per page. Every kit read goes through CS.budget : at most 2 in flight. A Mac that answers busy shows "Waiting for the Mac", never an error. A read frees its slot when it answers, when it is cancelled, or at the engine's 900-second backstop in the app (pass timeoutMs to an ask to change that). On a shared page each read also has the page's own limit of about 20 seconds; a read that goes over reads "The Mac didn't answer in time". Never a false zero. Show every figure through CS.value : known, Counting… , Loading… , Unknown · reason or Not loaded .

entries.title: Review the six states
entries.text: Review the six states Every dashboard is reviewed in six states, and ships a screenshot of each: cold : nothing cached. Skeletons and Counting… , never a zero. warm : the last answers are cached. The page paints them at once and says how old they are. section : a section is reading slowly. It shows "Still reading (N s)" with Cancel. switch : the selection changed. The shell stays; late answers for the old selection are dropped. offline : every read fails. The page shows its offline banner and keeps what it had. return : the page was hidden for ten minutes and is shown again. Zero reads, the DOM identical, scroll and focus kept. Source checkouts get scripts/lib/dashboard-state-fixtures.mjs ( stateFixture , bridgeScript , shootStates ) for a Playwright test on a virtual clock ( page.clock ), and scripts/lib/dashboard-check-rules.mjs for the source rules below.

entries.text: (b) Content folder: an agent writes a file, the page shows it The agent writes a JSON or Markdown file into a team content folder. If the agent writes with its own filesystem tools instead, it calls refresh_frontmatter_cache so the index sees the file. create_content_file The agent writes the feed. Use an absolute path inside the team's content folder; the example creates feeds/standup.json . With onCollision: "fail" a second create of the same path is refused; keep-both writes the next free numbered name instead. The tools are listed in Content file tools . { "tool": "create_content_file", "arguments": { "path": "/abs/context/_team/engineering/content/feeds/standup.json", "content": "{\"date\":\"2026-10-26\",\"items\":[\"Ship the docs page\",\"Review DEMO-27\"]}", "onCollision": "fail" } } The dashboard lists the folder, reads the file and re-renders when the folder changes. files.list returns {rows} (each row has id , path , name , kind ); pass a folder row's path as dir . files.read returns {text, truncated, size, sha256} .

entries.title: Which path to use
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Getting data into a dashboard
entries.text: Which path to use Path Pick it when Agent side In-app dashboard reads with Hosted dashboard reads with Engine query The data is something CodeSense already holds and must be live: sessions, inbox, runs, usage. Nothing to write. sessions() , inbox() , runs() , sessionUsage() , subscribe(topic) , onSessions , onInboxChanged The declared catalog queries sessions , inbox , runs , sessionUsage ; the inbox stream Content folder Anything else: a report, a feed, a JSON or Markdown file an agent produces. create_content_file into a team content folder files.list , files.read , subscribe('files') , queryContext , subscribeContext Frontmatter fields through queryContext only (no file text), or a data file listed in the manifest Records Many small structured items with named fields: tasks, events, checklist rows. records_create , records_write , records_set_fields subscribe('records', {collection}) , records.list , records.read Frontmatter fields through queryContext ; no collection selector, so mark each record with a shared field (see example c ) Core, fast data comes from the engine's queries. Everything else is content an agent writes, and the dashboard reads it back through the generic files and records reads, with no Rust change and no new query. In-app versus hosted An in-app dashboard runs in CodeSense on the Mac and has window.codesense . A published (hosted) dashboard has no window.codesense : it asks a fixed catalog of read-only queries through the live link and the Mac answers them. publish_dashboard refuses a page that calls window.codesense . Hosted answers are redacted and cut to fit 256 KB, each list query has its own row cap, and a hosted query is refreshed by polling no faster than every 15 seconds. Only the streams push. Private records and private notes are not reachable from a hosted dashboard at all: the hosted queryContext reads the dashboard's team content only. Build and check the page in-app first, then publish. Anything that depends on a verb or a field the hosted catalog does not offer will not…

entries.title: (a) Engine: recent sessions and the inbox
entries.crumb: CodeSense — Getting data into a dashboard
entries.text:
(a) Engine: recent sessions and the inbox Read the built-in sources directly. onSessions pushes the session list and calls back again on every change; inbox({limit}) returns the newest messages as {messages, hasMore} , and onInboxChanged tells you when to read again. Declare the grants in the page's meta tag ( Calling CodeSense lists them).
      The first-paint read and later changes both come from the same engine: you do not poll. subscribe('sessions') and subscribe('inbox') give the same data as topics with deltas; see LiveHub topics and rows . Always render message text with textContent . On a hosted dashboard the same sources are the catalog queries sessions and inbox , declared in the manifest's live block and read with CS.query or the inbox stream (see the "Agent builds a dashboard" handbook guide and get_live_data_contract , section hosted ).
